units.rightText: The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah

units.leftText: Oh clap your hands, all you nations. Shout to God with the voice of triumph!
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. Clap your hands, all you peoples; shout unto God with a voice of triumph.

units.leftText: For the LORD Most High is awesome. He is a great King over all the earth.
units.rightText: How awesome is the LORD Most High, the great King over all the earth!

units.leftText: He subdues nations under us, and peoples under our feet.
units.rightText: He subdues nations beneath us, and peoples under our feet.

units.leftText: He chooses our inheritance for us, the glory of Jacob whom he loved. Selah.*
units.rightText: He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob, whom He loves. Selah

units.leftText: God has gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet.
units.rightText: God has ascended amid shouts of joy, the LORD with the sound of the horn.

units.leftText: Sing praises to God! Sing praises! Sing praises to our King! Sing praises!
units.rightText: Sing praises to God, sing praises; sing praises to our King, sing praises!

units.leftText: For God is the King of all the earth. Sing praises with understanding.
units.rightText: For God is King of all the earth; sing to Him a psalm of praise.
rightNotes: 47:7 Or sing a Maskil of praise or sing praises with understanding

units.leftText: God reigns over the nations. God sits on his holy throne.
units.rightText: God reigns over the nations; God is seated on His holy throne.

units.leftText: The princes of the peoples are gathered together, the people of the God of Abraham. For the shields of the earth belong to God. He is greatly exalted!
units.rightText: The nobles of the nations have assembled as the people of the God of Abraham; for the shields of the earth belong to God; He is highly exalted.

units.leftText: Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised, in the city of our God, in his holy mountain.
units.rightText: A song. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, His holy mountain.

units.leftText: Beautiful in elevation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the north sides, the city of the great King.
units.rightText: Beautiful in loftiness, the joy of all the earth, like the peaks of Zaphon is Mount Zion, the city of the great King.
rightNotes: 48:2 Or in the far north; the most sacred mountain of the Canaanites was Zaphon

units.leftText: God has shown himself in her citadels as a refuge.
units.rightText: God is in her citadels; He has shown Himself to be a fortress.

units.leftText: For, behold, the kings assembled themselves, they passed by together.
units.rightText: For behold, the kings assembled; they all advanced together.

units.leftText: They saw it, then they were amazed. They were dismayed. They hurried away.
units.rightText: They saw and were astounded; they fled in terror.

units.leftText: Trembling took hold of them there, pain, as of a woman in travail.
units.rightText: Trembling seized them there, anguish like a woman in labor.

units.leftText: With the east wind, you break the ships of Tarshish.
units.rightText: With a wind from the east You wrecked the ships of Tarshish.
rightNotes: 48:7 Or a fleet of trading ships

units.leftText: As we have heard, so we have seen, in the city of the LORD of Armies, in the city of our God. God will establish it forever. Selah.*
units.rightText: As we have heard, so we have seen in the city of the LORD of Hosts, in the city of our God: God will establish her forever. Selah

units.leftText: We have thought about your loving kindness, God, in the middle of your temple.
units.rightText: Within Your temple, O God, we contemplate Your loving devotion.

units.leftText: As is your name, God, so is your praise to the ends of the earth. Your right hand is full of righteousness.
units.rightText: Your name, O God, like Your praise, reaches to the ends of the earth; Your right hand is full of righteousness.

units.leftText: Let Mount Zion be glad! Let the daughters of Judah rejoice because of your judgments.
units.rightText: Mount Zion is glad, the daughters of Judah rejoice, on account of Your judgments.
rightNotes: 48:11 Or the villages

units.leftText: Walk about Zion, and go around her. Number its towers.
units.rightText: March around Zion, encircle her, count her towers,

units.leftText: Notice her bulwarks. Consider her palaces, that you may tell it to the next generation.
units.rightText: consider her ramparts, tour her citadels, that you may tell the next generation.

units.leftText: For this God is our God forever and ever. He will be our guide even to death.
units.rightText: For this God is our God forever and ever; He will be our guide even till death.
rightNotes: 48:14 Or He will guide us beyond death

units.leftText: Hear this, all you peoples. Listen, all you inhabitants of the world,
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. Hear this, all you peoples; listen, all inhabitants of the world,

units.leftText: both low and high, rich and poor together.
units.rightText: both low and high, rich and poor alike.

units.leftText: My mouth will speak words of wisdom. My heart will utter understanding.
units.rightText: My mouth will impart wisdom, and the meditation of my heart will bring understanding.

units.leftText: I will incline my ear to a proverb. I will solve my riddle on the harp.
units.rightText: I will incline my ear to a proverb; I will express my riddle with the harp:

units.leftText: Why should I fear in the days of evil, when iniquity at my heels surrounds me?
units.rightText: Why should I fear in times of trouble, when wicked usurpers surround me?

units.leftText: Those who trust in their wealth, and boast in the multitude of their riches—
units.rightText: They trust in their wealth and boast in their great riches.

units.leftText: none of them can by any means redeem his brother, nor give God a ransom for him.
units.rightText: No man can possibly redeem his brother or pay his ransom to God.
rightNotes: 49:7 Or redeem another

units.leftText: For the redemption of their life is costly, no payment is ever enough,
units.rightText: For the redemption of his soul is costly, and never can payment suffice,

units.leftText: that he should live on forever, that he should not see corruption.
units.rightText: that he should live on forever and not see decay.

units.leftText: For he sees that wise men die; likewise the fool and the senseless perish, and leave their wealth to others.
units.rightText: For it is clear that wise men die, and the foolish and the senseless both perish and leave their wealth to others.

units.leftText: Their inward thought is that their houses will endure forever, and their dwelling places to all generations. They name their lands after themselves.
units.rightText: Their graves are their eternal homes — their dwellings for endless generations — even though their lands were their namesakes.
rightNotes: 49:11 LXX, Syriac, and Aramaic Targum; Hebrew Their inward thoughts

units.leftText: But man, despite his riches, doesn’t endure. He is like the animals that perish.
units.rightText: But a man, despite his wealth, cannot endure; he is like the beasts that perish.

units.leftText: This is the destiny of those who are foolish, and of those who approve their sayings. Selah.*
units.rightText: This is the fate of the foolish and their followers who endorse their sayings. Selah
rightNotes: 49:13 Or the way of the foolish

units.leftText: They are appointed as a flock for Sheol. Death shall be their shepherd. The upright shall have dominion over them in the morning. Their beauty shall decay in Sheol, far from their mansion.
units.rightText: Like sheep they are destined for Sheol. Death will be their shepherd. The upright will rule them in the morning, and their form will decay in Sheol, far from their lofty abode.
leftNotes: 49:14 Sheol is the place of the dead.
49:14 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: But God will redeem my soul from the power of Sheol, for he will receive me. Selah.*
units.rightText: But God will redeem my life from Sheol, for He will surely take me to Himself. Selah
leftNotes: 49:15 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: Don’t be afraid when a man is made rich, when the glory of his house is increased;
units.rightText: Do not be afraid when a man grows rich, when the splendor of his house increases.

units.leftText: for when he dies he will carry nothing away. His glory won’t descend after him.
units.rightText: For when he dies, he will carry nothing away; his abundance will not follow him down.

units.leftText: Though while he lived he blessed his soul— and men praise you when you do well for yourself—
units.rightText: Though in his lifetime he blesses his soul — and men praise you when you prosper —

units.leftText: he shall go to the generation of his fathers. They shall never see the light.
units.rightText: he will join the generation of his fathers, who will never see the light of day.

units.leftText: A man who has riches without understanding, is like the animals that perish.
units.rightText: A man who has riches without understanding is like the beasts that perish.

units.leftText: The Mighty One, God, the LORD, speaks, and calls the earth from sunrise to sunset.
units.rightText: A Psalm of Asaph. The Mighty One, God the LORD, speaks and summons the earth from where the sun rises to where it sets.

units.leftText: Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God shines out.
units.rightText: From Zion, perfect in beauty, God shines forth.

units.leftText: Our God comes, and does not keep silent. A fire devours before him. It is very stormy around him.
units.rightText: Our God approaches and will not be silent! Consuming fire precedes Him, and a tempest rages around Him.

units.leftText: He calls to the heavens above, to the earth, that he may judge his people:
units.rightText: He summons the heavens above, and the earth, that He may judge His people:

units.leftText: “Gather my saints together to me, those who have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.”
units.rightText: “Gather to Me My saints, who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice.”

units.leftText: The heavens shall declare his righteousness, for God himself is judge. Selah.*
units.rightText: And the heavens proclaim His righteousness, for God Himself is Judge. Selah
rightNotes: 50:6 Or He is a God of justice

units.leftText: “Hear, my people, and I will speak. Israel, I will testify against you. I am God, your God.
units.rightText: “Hear, O My people, and I will speak, O Israel, and I will testify against you: I am God, your God.

units.leftText: I don’t rebuke you for your sacrifices. Your burnt offerings are continually before me.
units.rightText: I do not rebuke you for your sacrifices, and your burnt offerings are ever before Me.

units.leftText: I have no need for a bull from your stall, nor male goats from your pens.
units.rightText: I have no need for a bull from your stall or goats from your pens,

units.leftText: For every animal of the forest is mine, and the livestock on a thousand hills.
units.rightText: for every beast of the forest is Mine — the cattle on a thousand hills.

units.leftText: I know all the birds of the mountains. The wild animals of the field are mine.
units.rightText: I know every bird in the mountains, and the creatures of the field are Mine.

units.leftText: If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is mine, and all that is in it.
units.rightText: If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is Mine, and the fullness thereof.

units.leftText: Will I eat the meat of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
units.rightText: Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?

units.leftText: Offer to God the sacrifice of thanksgiving. Pay your vows to the Most High.
units.rightText: Sacrifice a thank offering to God, and fulfill your vows to the Most High.

units.leftText: Call on me in the day of trouble. I will deliver you, and you will honor me.”
units.rightText: Call upon Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you will honor Me.”

units.leftText: But to the wicked God says, “What right do you have to declare my statutes, that you have taken my covenant on your lips,
units.rightText: To the wicked, however, God says, “What right have you to recite My statutes and to bear My covenant on your lips?

units.leftText: since you hate instruction, and throw my words behind you?
units.rightText: For you hate My instruction and cast My words behind you.

units.leftText: When you saw a thief, you consented with him, and have participated with adulterers.
units.rightText: When you see a thief, you befriend him, and throw in your lot with adulterers.

units.leftText: “You give your mouth to evil. Your tongue frames deceit.
units.rightText: You unleash your mouth for evil and harness your tongue to deceit.

units.leftText: You sit and speak against your brother. You slander your own mother’s son.
units.rightText: You sit and malign your brother; you slander your own mother’s son.

units.leftText: You have done these things, and I kept silent. You thought that I was just like you. I will rebuke you, and accuse you in front of your eyes.
units.rightText: You have done these things, and I kept silent; you thought I was just like you. But now I rebuke you and accuse you to your face.
rightNotes: 50:21 Or you thought the ‘I AM’ was
50:21 Literally and I set it in order before your eyes

units.leftText: “Now consider this, you who forget God, lest I tear you into pieces, and there be no one to deliver.
units.rightText: Now consider this, you who forget God, lest I tear you to pieces, with no one to rescue you:

units.leftText: Whoever offers the sacrifice of thanksgiving glorifies me, and prepares his way so that I will show God’s salvation to him.”
units.rightText: He who sacrifices a thank offering honors Me, and to him who rightly orders his way, I will show the salvation of God.”

units.leftText: Have mercy on me, God, according to your loving kindness. According to the multitude of your tender mercies, blot out my transgressions.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. When Nathan the prophet came to him after his adultery with Bathsheba. Have mercy on me, O God, according to Your loving devotion; according to Your great compassion, blot out my transgressions.
rightNotes: 51:1 Or Be gracious to me

units.leftText: Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity. Cleanse me from my sin.
units.rightText: Wash me clean of my iniquity and cleanse me from my sin.

units.leftText: For I know my transgressions. My sin is constantly before me.
units.rightText: For I know my transgressions, and my sin is always before me.

units.leftText: Against you, and you only, I have sinned, and done that which is evil in your sight, so you may be proved right when you speak, and justified when you judge.
units.rightText: Against You, You only, have I sinned and done what is evil in Your sight, so that You may be proved right when You speak and blameless when You judge.
rightNotes: 51:4 LXX and victorious when You judge; cited in Romans 3:4|ROM 3:4*

units.leftText: Behold, I was born in iniquity. My mother conceived me in sin.
units.rightText: Surely I was brought forth in iniquity; I was sinful when my mother conceived me.

units.leftText: Behold, you desire truth in the inward parts. You teach me wisdom in the inmost place.
units.rightText: Surely You desire truth in the inmost being; You teach me wisdom in the inmost place.

units.leftText: Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean. Wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
units.rightText: Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.

units.leftText: Let me hear joy and gladness, that the bones which you have broken may rejoice.
units.rightText: Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones You have crushed rejoice.

units.leftText: Hide your face from my sins, and blot out all of my iniquities.
units.rightText: Hide Your face from my sins and blot out all my iniquities.

units.leftText: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.
units.rightText: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.

units.leftText: Don’t throw me from your presence, and don’t take your Holy Spirit from me.
units.rightText: Cast me not away from Your presence; take not Your Holy Spirit from me.

units.leftText: Restore to me the joy of your salvation. Uphold me with a willing spirit.
units.rightText: Restore to me the joy of Your salvation, and sustain me with a willing spirit.

units.leftText: Then I will teach transgressors your ways. Sinners will be converted to you.
units.rightText: Then I will teach transgressors Your ways, and sinners will return to You.

units.leftText: Deliver me from the guilt of bloodshed, O God, the God of my salvation. My tongue will sing aloud of your righteousness.
units.rightText: Deliver me from bloodguilt, O God, the God of my salvation, and my tongue will sing of Your righteousness.

units.leftText: Lord, open my lips. My mouth will declare your praise.
units.rightText: O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise.

units.leftText: For you don’t delight in sacrifice, or else I would give it. You have no pleasure in burnt offering.
units.rightText: For You do not delight in sacrifice, or I would bring it; You take no pleasure in burnt offerings.

units.leftText: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit. O God, you will not despise a broken and contrite heart.
units.rightText: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.

units.leftText: Do well in your good pleasure to Zion. Build the walls of Jerusalem.
units.rightText: In Your good pleasure, cause Zion to prosper; build up the walls of Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Then you will delight in the sacrifices of righteousness, in burnt offerings and in whole burnt offerings. Then they will offer bulls on your altar.
units.rightText: Then You will delight in righteous sacrifices, in whole burnt offerings; then bulls will be offered on Your altar.

units.leftText: Why do you boast of mischief, mighty man? God’s loving kindness endures continually.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. A Maskil of David. After Doeg the Edomite went to Saul and told him, “David has gone to the house of Ahimelech.” Why do you boast of evil, O mighty man? The loving devotion of God endures all day long.
rightNotes: 52:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142.

units.leftText: Your tongue plots destruction, like a sharp razor, working deceitfully.
units.rightText: Your tongue devises destruction like a sharpened razor, O worker of deceit.

units.leftText: You love evil more than good, lying rather than speaking the truth. Selah.*
units.rightText: You love evil more than good, falsehood more than speaking truth. Selah

units.leftText: You love all devouring words, you deceitful tongue.
units.rightText: You love every word that devours, O deceitful tongue.

units.leftText: God will likewise destroy you forever. He will take you up, and pluck you out of your tent, and root you out of the land of the living. Selah.*
units.rightText: Surely God will bring you down to everlasting ruin; He will snatch you up and tear you away from your tent; He will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah

units.leftText: The righteous also will see it, and fear, and laugh at him, saying,
units.rightText: The righteous will see and fear; they will mock the evildoer, saying,

units.leftText: “Behold, this is the man who didn’t make God his strength, but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened himself in his wickedness.”
units.rightText: “Look at the man who did not make God his refuge, but trusted in the abundance of his wealth and strengthened himself by destruction.”

units.leftText: But as for me, I am like a green olive tree in God’s house. I trust in God’s loving kindness forever and ever.
units.rightText: But I am like an olive tree flourishing in the house of God; I trust in the loving devotion of God forever and ever.

units.leftText: I will give you thanks forever, because you have done it. I will hope in your name, for it is good, in the presence of your saints.
units.rightText: I will praise You forever, because You have done it. I will wait on Your name — for it is good — in the presence of Your saints.

units.leftText: The fool has said in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt, and have done abominable iniquity. There is no one who does good.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. According to Mahalath. A Maskil of David. The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt; their ways are vile. There is no one who does good.
rightNotes: 53:1 Mahalathis probably a musical or liturgical term; see also Psalm 88:1|PSA 88:1*.
53:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142.

units.leftText: God looks down from heaven on the children of men, to see if there are any who understood, who seek after God.
units.rightText: God looks down from heaven upon the sons of men to see if any understand, if any seek God.

units.leftText: Every one of them has gone back. They have become filthy together. There is no one who does good, no, not one.
units.rightText: All have turned away, they have together become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one.
rightNotes: 53:3 LXX worthless
53:3 Cited in Romans 3:10–12|ROM 3:10-12*

units.leftText: Have the workers of iniquity no knowledge, who eat up my people as they eat bread, and don’t call on God?
units.rightText: Will the workers of iniquity never learn? They devour my people like bread; they refuse to call upon God.

units.leftText: There they were in great fear, where no fear was, for God has scattered the bones of him who encamps against you. You have put them to shame, because God has rejected them.
units.rightText: There they are, overwhelmed with dread, where there was nothing to fear. For God has scattered the bones of those who besieged you. You put them to shame, for God has despised them.

units.leftText: Oh that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion! When God brings back his people from captivity, then Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.
units.rightText: Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come from Zion! When God restores His captive people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad!
rightNotes: 53:6 Or the fortunes of His people

units.leftText: Save me, God, by your name. Vindicate me in your might.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Maskil of David. When the Ziphites went to Saul and said, “Is David not hiding among us?” Save me, O God, by Your name, and vindicate me by Your might!
rightNotes: 54:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142.

units.leftText: Hear my prayer, God. Listen to the words of my mouth.
units.rightText: Hear my prayer, O God; listen to the words of my mouth.

units.leftText: For strangers have risen up against me. Violent men have sought after my soul. They haven’t set God before them. Selah.*
units.rightText: For strangers rise up against me, and ruthless men seek my life — men with no regard for God. Selah

units.leftText: Behold, God is my helper. The Lord is the one who sustains my soul.
units.rightText: Surely God is my helper; the Lord is the sustainer of my soul.

units.leftText: He will repay the evil to my enemies. Destroy them in your truth.
units.rightText: He will reward my enemies with evil. In Your faithfulness, destroy them.

units.leftText: With a free will offering, I will sacrifice to you. I will give thanks to your name, LORD, for it is good.
units.rightText: Freely I will sacrifice to You; I will praise Your name, O LORD, for it is good.

units.leftText: For he has delivered me out of all trouble. My eye has seen triumph over my enemies.
units.rightText: For He has delivered me from every trouble, and my eyes have looked in triumph on my foes.

units.leftText: Listen to my prayer, God. Don’t hide yourself from my supplication.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Maskil of David. Listen to my prayer, O God, and do not ignore my plea.
rightNotes: 55:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142.

units.leftText: Attend to me, and answer me. I am restless in my complaint, and moan
units.rightText: Attend to me and answer me. I am restless in my complaint,

units.leftText: because of the voice of the enemy, because of the oppression of the wicked. For they bring suffering on me. In anger they hold a grudge against me.
units.rightText: at the voice of the enemy, at the pressure of the wicked. For they bring down disaster upon me and resent me in their anger.

units.leftText: My heart is severely pained within me. The terrors of death have fallen on me.
units.rightText: My heart pounds within me, and the terrors of death assail me.

units.leftText: Fearfulness and trembling have come on me. Horror has overwhelmed me.
units.rightText: Fear and trembling grip me, and horror has overwhelmed me.

units.leftText: I said, “Oh that I had wings like a dove! Then I would fly away, and be at rest.
units.rightText: I said, “Oh, that I had wings like a dove! I would fly away and find rest.

units.leftText: Behold, then I would wander far off. I would lodge in the wilderness.” Selah.*
units.rightText: How far away I would flee! In the wilderness I would remain. Selah

units.leftText: “I would hurry to a shelter from the stormy wind and storm.”
units.rightText: I would hurry to my shelter, far from this raging tempest.”

units.leftText: Confuse them, Lord, and confound their language, for I have seen violence and strife in the city.
units.rightText: O Lord, confuse and confound their speech, for I see violence and strife in the city.

units.leftText: Day and night they prowl around on its walls. Malice and abuse are also within her.
units.rightText: Day and night they encircle the walls, while malice and trouble lie within.

units.leftText: Destructive forces are within her. Threats and lies don’t depart from her streets.
units.rightText: Destruction is within; oppression and deceit never leave the streets.

units.leftText: For it was not an enemy who insulted me, then I could have endured it. Neither was it he who hated me who raised himself up against me, then I would have hidden myself from him.
units.rightText: For it is not an enemy who insults me; that I could endure. It is not a foe who rises against me; from him I could hide.

units.leftText: But it was you, a man like me, my companion, and my familiar friend.
units.rightText: But it is you, a man like myself, my companion and close friend.

units.leftText: We took sweet fellowship together. We walked in God’s house with company.
units.rightText: We shared sweet fellowship together; we walked with the crowd into the house of God.

units.leftText: Let death come suddenly on them. Let them go down alive into Sheol. For wickedness is among them, in their dwelling.
units.rightText: Let death seize them by surprise; let them go down to Sheol alive, for evil is with them in their homes.
leftNotes: 55:15 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: As for me, I will call on God. The LORD will save me.
units.rightText: But I call to God, and the LORD saves me.

units.leftText: Evening, morning, and at noon, I will cry out in distress. He will hear my voice.
units.rightText: Morning, noon, and night, I cry out in distress, and He hears my voice.

units.leftText: He has redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me, although there are many who oppose me.
units.rightText: He redeems my soul in peace from the battle waged against me, even though many oppose me.

units.leftText: God, who is enthroned forever, will hear and answer them. Selah.* They never change and don’t fear God.
units.rightText: God will hear and humiliate them — the One enthroned for the ages — Selah because they do not change and they have no fear of God.

units.leftText: He raises his hands against his friends. He has violated his covenant.
units.rightText: My companion attacks his friends; he violates his covenant.

units.leftText: His mouth was smooth as butter, but his heart was war. His words were softer than oil, yet they were drawn swords.
units.rightText: His speech is smooth as butter, but war is in his heart. His words are softer than oil, yet they are swords unsheathed.

units.leftText: Cast your burden on the LORD and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be moved.
units.rightText: Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you; He will never let the righteous be shaken.

units.leftText: But you, God, will bring them down into the pit of destruction. Bloodthirsty and deceitful men shall not live out half their days, but I will trust in you.
units.rightText: But You, O God, will bring them down to the Pit of destruction; men of bloodshed and deceit will not live out half their days. But I will trust in You.

units.leftText: Be merciful to me, God, for man wants to swallow me up. All day long, he attacks and oppresses me.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “A Dove on Distant Oaks.” A Miktam of David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath. Be merciful to me, O God, for men are hounding me; all day they press their attack.
rightNotes: 56:1 Miktam is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 16 and 56–60.

units.leftText: My enemies want to swallow me up all day long, for they are many who fight proudly against me.
units.rightText: My enemies pursue me all day long, for many proudly assail me.

units.leftText: When I am afraid, I will put my trust in you.
units.rightText: When I am afraid, I put my trust in You.

units.leftText: In God, I praise his word. In God, I put my trust. I will not be afraid. What can flesh do to me?
units.rightText: In God, whose word I praise — in God I trust. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?

units.leftText: All day long they twist my words. All their thoughts are against me for evil.
units.rightText: All day long they twist my words; all their thoughts are on my demise.

units.leftText: They conspire and lurk, watching my steps. They are eager to take my life.
units.rightText: They conspire, they lurk, they watch my steps while they wait to take my life.

units.leftText: Shall they escape by iniquity? In anger cast down the peoples, God.
units.rightText: In spite of such sin, will they escape? In Your anger, O God, cast down the nations.
rightNotes: 56:7 Or do not let them escape; MT does not include do not.

units.leftText: You count my wanderings. You put my tears into your container. Aren’t they in your book?
units.rightText: You have taken account of my wanderings. Put my tears in Your bottle — are they not in Your book?
rightNotes: 56:8 Or sorrows

units.leftText: Then my enemies shall turn back in the day that I call. I know this: that God is for me.
units.rightText: Then my enemies will retreat on the day I cry for help. By this I will know that God is on my side.

units.leftText: In God, I will praise his word. In the LORD, I will praise his word.
units.rightText: In God, whose word I praise, in the LORD, whose word I praise,

units.leftText: I have put my trust in God. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
units.rightText: in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?

units.leftText: Your vows are on me, God. I will give thank offerings to you.
units.rightText: Your vows are upon me, O God; I will render thank offerings to You.

units.leftText: For you have delivered my soul from death, and prevented my feet from falling, that I may walk before God in the light of the living.
units.rightText: For You have delivered my soul from death, and my feet from stumbling, that I may walk before God in the light of life.

units.leftText: Be merciful to me, God, be merciful to me, for my soul takes refuge in you. Yes, in the shadow of your wings, I will take refuge, until disaster has passed.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David, when he fled from Saul into the cave. Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy, for in You my soul takes refuge. In the shadow of Your wings I will take shelter until the danger has passed.
rightNotes: 57:1 Miktam is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 16 and 56–60.

units.leftText: I cry out to God Most High, to God who accomplishes my requests for me.
units.rightText: I cry out to God Most High, to God who fulfills His purpose for me.
rightNotes: 57:2 Hebrew Elohim-Elyon

units.leftText: He will send from heaven, and save me, he rebukes the one who is pursuing me. Selah.* God will send out his loving kindness and his truth.
units.rightText: He reaches down from heaven and saves me; He rebukes those who trample me. Selah God sends forth His loving devotion and His truth.

units.leftText: My soul is among lions. I lie among those who are set on fire, even the sons of men, whose teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword.
units.rightText: My soul is among the lions; I lie down with ravenous beasts— with men whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are sharp swords.

units.leftText: Be exalted, God, above the heavens! Let your glory be above all the earth!
units.rightText: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth.

units.leftText: They have prepared a net for my steps. My soul is bowed down. They dig a pit before me. They fall into the middle of it themselves. Selah.*
units.rightText: They spread a net for my feet; my soul was despondent. They dug a pit before me, but they themselves have fallen into it! Selah

units.leftText: My heart is steadfast, God. My heart is steadfast. I will sing, yes, I will sing praises.
units.rightText: My heart is steadfast, O God, my heart is steadfast. I will sing and make music.

units.leftText: Wake up, my glory! Wake up, lute and harp! I will wake up the dawn.
units.rightText: Awake, my glory! Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn.
rightNotes: 57:8 Or Awake, my soul!

units.leftText: I will give thanks to you, Lord, among the peoples. I will sing praises to you among the nations.
units.rightText: I will praise You, O Lord, among the nations; I will sing Your praises among the peoples.

units.leftText: For your great loving kindness reaches to the heavens, and your truth to the skies.
units.rightText: For Your loving devotion reaches to the heavens, and Your faithfulness to the clouds.

units.leftText: Be exalted, God, above the heavens. Let your glory be over all the earth.
units.rightText: Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth.

units.leftText: Do you indeed speak righteousness, silent ones? Do you judge blamelessly, you sons of men?
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David. Do you indeed speak justly, O rulers? Do you judge uprightly, O sons of men?
rightNotes: 58:1 Miktam is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 16 and 56–60.

units.leftText: No, in your heart you plot injustice. You measure out the violence of your hands on the earth.
units.rightText: No, in your hearts you devise injustice; with your hands you mete out violence on the earth.

units.leftText: The wicked go astray from the womb. They are wayward as soon as they are born, speaking lies.
units.rightText: The wicked are estranged from the womb; the liars go astray from birth.

units.leftText: Their poison is like the poison of a snake, like a deaf cobra that stops its ear,
units.rightText: Their venom is like the venom of a snake, like a cobra that shuts its ears,

units.leftText: which doesn’t listen to the voice of charmers, no matter how skillful the charmer may be.
units.rightText: refusing to hear the tune of the charmer who skillfully weaves his spell.

units.leftText: Break their teeth, God, in their mouth. Break out the great teeth of the young lions, LORD.
units.rightText: O God, shatter their teeth in their mouths; O LORD, tear out the fangs of the lions.

units.leftText: Let them vanish like water that flows away. When they draw the bow, let their arrows be made blunt.
units.rightText: May they vanish like water that runs off; when they draw the bow, may their arrows be blunted.
rightNotes: 58:7 Or when they are trodden down, may they wither like grass

units.leftText: Let them be like a snail which melts and passes away, like the stillborn child, who has not seen the sun.
units.rightText: Like a slug that dissolves in its slime, like a woman’s stillborn child, may they never see the sun.

units.leftText: Before your pots can feel the heat of the thorns, he will sweep away the green and the burning alike.
units.rightText: Before your pots can feel the burning thorns— whether green or dry— He will sweep them away.

units.leftText: The righteous shall rejoice when he sees the vengeance. He shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked,
units.rightText: The righteous will rejoice when they see they are avenged; they will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.

units.leftText: so that men shall say, “Most certainly there is a reward for the righteous. Most certainly there is a God who judges the earth.”
units.rightText: Then men will say, “There is surely a reward for the righteous! There is surely a God who judges the earth!”

units.leftText: Deliver me from my enemies, my God. Set me on high from those who rise up against me.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David, when Saul sent men to watch David’s house in order to kill him. Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; protect me from those who rise against me.
rightNotes: 59:1 Miktam is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 16 and 56–60.

units.leftText: Deliver me from the workers of iniquity. Save me from the bloodthirsty men.
units.rightText: Deliver me from workers of iniquity, and save me from men of bloodshed.

units.leftText: For, behold, they lie in wait for my soul. The mighty gather themselves together against me, not for my disobedience, nor for my sin, LORD.
units.rightText: See how they lie in wait for me. Fierce men conspire against me for no transgression or sin of my own, O LORD.

units.leftText: I have done no wrong, yet they are ready to attack me. Rise up, behold, and help me!
units.rightText: For no fault of my own, they move swiftly to attack me. Arise to help me, and take notice.

units.leftText: You, LORD God of Armies, the God of Israel, rouse yourself to punish the nations. Show no mercy to the wicked traitors. Selah.*
units.rightText: O LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel, rouse Yourself to punish all the nations; show no mercy to the wicked traitors. Selah

units.leftText: They return at evening, howling like dogs, and prowl around the city.
units.rightText: They return in the evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the city.

units.leftText: Behold, they spew with their mouth. Swords are in their lips, “For”, they say, “who hears us?”
units.rightText: See what they spew from their mouths— sharp words from their lips: “For who can hear us?”

units.leftText: But you, LORD, laugh at them. You scoff at all the nations.
units.rightText: But You, O LORD, laugh at them; You scoff at all the nations.

units.leftText: Oh, my Strength, I watch for you, for God is my high tower.
units.rightText: I will keep watch for You, O my strength, because You, O God, are my fortress.

units.leftText: My God will go before me with his loving kindness. God will let me look at my enemies in triumph.
units.rightText: My God of loving devotion will come to meet me; God will let me stare down my foes.

units.leftText: Don’t kill them, or my people may forget. Scatter them by your power, and bring them down, Lord our shield.
units.rightText: Do not kill them, or my people will forget. Scatter them by Your power, and bring them down, O Lord, our shield.

units.leftText: For the sin of their mouth, and the words of their lips, let them be caught in their pride, for the curses and lies which they utter.
units.rightText: By the sins of their mouths and the words of their lips, let them be trapped in their pride, in the curses and lies they utter.

units.leftText: Consume them in wrath. Consume them, and they will be no more. Let them know that God rules in Jacob, to the ends of the earth. Selah.*
units.rightText: Consume them in wrath; consume them till they are no more, so it may be known to the ends of the earth that God rules over Jacob. Selah

units.leftText: At evening let them return. Let them howl like a dog, and go around the city.
units.rightText: They return in the evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the city.

units.leftText: They shall wander up and down for food, and wait all night if they aren’t satisfied.
units.rightText: They scavenge for food, and growl if they are not satisfied.

units.leftText: But I will sing of your strength. Yes, I will sing aloud of your loving kindness in the morning. For you have been my high tower, a refuge in the day of my distress.
units.rightText: But I will sing of Your strength and proclaim Your loving devotion in the morning. For You are my fortress, my refuge in times of trouble.

units.leftText: To you, my strength, I will sing praises. For God is my high tower, the God of my mercy.
units.rightText: To You, O my strength, I sing praises, for You, O God, are my fortress, my God of loving devotion.

units.leftText: God, you have rejected us. You have broken us down. You have been angry. Restore us, again.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Lily of the Covenant.” A Miktam of David for instruction. When he fought Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and struck down 12,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. You have rejected us, O God; You have broken us; You have been angry; restore us!
rightNotes: 60:1 Miktam is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 16 and 56–60.
60:1 That is, Mesopotamia; Aram-naharaim means Aram of the two rivers, likely the region between the Euphrates and Balih Rivers in northwestern Mesopotamia.
60:1 That is, the land northeast of Damascus

units.leftText: You have made the land tremble. You have torn it. Mend its fractures, for it quakes.
units.rightText: You have shaken the land and torn it open. Heal its fractures, for it is quaking.

units.leftText: You have shown your people hard things. You have made us drink the wine that makes us stagger.
units.rightText: You have shown Your people hardship; we are staggered from the wine You made us drink.

units.leftText: You have given a banner to those who fear you, that it may be displayed because of the truth. Selah.*
units.rightText: You have raised a banner for those who fear You, that they may flee the bow. Selah
rightNotes: 60:4 Or that it may be displayed because of truth

units.leftText: So that your beloved may be delivered, save with your right hand, and answer us.
units.rightText: Respond and save us with Your right hand, that Your beloved may be delivered.

units.leftText: God has spoken from his sanctuary: “I will triumph. I will divide Shechem, and measure out the valley of Succoth.
units.rightText: God has spoken from His sanctuary: “I will triumph! I will parcel out Shechem and apportion the Valley of Succoth.
rightNotes: 60:6 Or in His holiness

units.leftText: Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine. Ephraim also is the defense of my head. Judah is my scepter.
units.rightText: Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh is Mine; Ephraim is My helmet, Judah is My scepter.

units.leftText: Moab is my wash basin. I will throw my sandal on Edom. I shout in triumph over Philistia.”
units.rightText: Moab is My washbasin; upon Edom I toss My sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph.”

units.leftText: Who will bring me into the strong city? Who has led me to Edom?
units.rightText: Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?

units.leftText: Haven’t you, God, rejected us? You don’t go out with our armies, God.
units.rightText: Have You not rejected us, O God? Will You no longer march out, O God, with our armies?

units.leftText: Give us help against the adversary, for the help of man is vain.
units.rightText: Give us aid against the enemy, for the help of man is worthless.

units.leftText: Through God we will do valiantly, for it is he who will tread down our adversaries.
units.rightText: With God we will perform with valor, and He will trample our enemies.

units.leftText: Hear my cry, God. Listen to my prayer.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. Of David. Hear my cry, O God; attend to my prayer.

units.leftText: From the end of the earth, I will call to you when my heart is overwhelmed. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
units.rightText: From the ends of the earth I call out to You whenever my heart is faint. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.

units.leftText: For you have been a refuge for me, a strong tower from the enemy.
units.rightText: For You have been my refuge, a tower of strength against the enemy.

units.leftText: I will dwell in your tent forever. I will take refuge in the shelter of your wings. Selah.*
units.rightText: Let me dwell in Your tent forever and take refuge in the shelter of Your wings. Selah

units.leftText: For you, God, have heard my vows. You have given me the heritage of those who fear your name.
units.rightText: For You have heard my vows, O God; You have given me the inheritance reserved for those who fear Your name.

units.leftText: You will prolong the king’s life. His years will be for generations.
units.rightText: Increase the days of the king’s life; may his years span many generations.

units.leftText: He shall be enthroned in God’s presence forever. Appoint your loving kindness and truth, that they may preserve him.
units.rightText: May he sit enthroned in God’s presence forever; appoint Your loving devotion and Your faithfulness to guard him.

units.leftText: So I will sing praise to your name forever, that I may fulfill my vows daily.
units.rightText: Then I will ever sing praise to Your name and fulfill my vows day by day.

units.leftText: My soul rests in God alone. My salvation is from him.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. According to Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. In God alone my soul finds rest; my salvation comes from Him.

units.leftText: He alone is my rock, my salvation, and my fortress. I will never be greatly shaken.
units.rightText: He alone is my rock and my salvation. He is my fortress; I will never be shaken.

units.leftText: How long will you assault a man? Would all of you throw him down, like a leaning wall, like a tottering fence?
units.rightText: How long will you threaten a man? Will all of you throw him down like a leaning wall or a tottering fence?

units.leftText: They fully intend to throw him down from his lofty place. They delight in lies. They bless with their mouth, but they curse inwardly. Selah.*
units.rightText: They fully intend to cast him down from his lofty perch; they delight in lies; with their mouths they bless, but inwardly they curse. Selah

units.leftText: My soul, wait in silence for God alone, for my expectation is from him.
units.rightText: Rest in God alone, O my soul, for my hope comes from Him.

units.leftText: He alone is my rock and my salvation, my fortress. I will not be shaken.
units.rightText: He alone is my rock and my salvation; He is my fortress; I will not be shaken.

units.leftText: My salvation and my honor is with God. The rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God.
units.rightText: My salvation and my honor rest on God, my strong rock; my refuge is in God.

units.leftText: Trust in him at all times, you people. Pour out your heart before him. God is a refuge for us. Selah.*
units.rightText: Trust in Him at all times, O people; pour out your hearts before Him. God is our refuge. Selah

units.leftText: Surely men of low degree are just a breath, and men of high degree are a lie. In the balances they will go up. They are together lighter than a breath.
units.rightText: Lowborn men are but a vapor; the exalted are but a lie. Weighed on the scale, they go up; together they are but a vapor.

units.leftText: Don’t trust in oppression. Don’t become vain in robbery. If riches increase, don’t set your heart on them.
units.rightText: Place no trust in extortion or false hope in stolen goods. If your riches increase, do not set your heart upon them.

units.leftText: God has spoken once; twice I have heard this, that power belongs to God.
units.rightText: God has spoken once; I have heard this twice: that power belongs to God,

units.leftText: Also to you, Lord, belongs loving kindness, for you reward every man according to his work.
units.rightText: and loving devotion to You, O Lord. For You will repay each man according to his deeds.
rightNotes: 62:12 Cited in Romans 2:6|ROM 2:6*

units.leftText: God, you are my God. I will earnestly seek you. My soul thirsts for you. My flesh longs for you, in a dry and weary land, where there is no water.
units.rightText: A Psalm of David, when he was in the Wilderness of Judah. O God, You are my God. Earnestly I seek You; my soul thirsts for You. My body yearns for You in a dry and weary land without water.

units.leftText: So I have seen you in the sanctuary, watching your power and your glory.
units.rightText: So I have seen You in the sanctuary and beheld Your power and glory.

units.leftText: Because your loving kindness is better than life, my lips shall praise you.
units.rightText: Because Your loving devotion is better than life, my lips will glorify You.

units.leftText: So I will bless you while I live. I will lift up my hands in your name.
units.rightText: So I will bless You as long as I live; in Your name I will lift my hands.

units.leftText: My soul shall be satisfied as with the richest food. My mouth shall praise you with joyful lips,
units.rightText: My soul is satisfied as with the richest of foods; with joyful lips my mouth will praise You.

units.leftText: when I remember you on my bed, and think about you in the night watches.
units.rightText: When I remember You on my bed, I think of You through the watches of the night.

units.leftText: For you have been my help. I will rejoice in the shadow of your wings.
units.rightText: For You are my help; I will sing for joy in the shadow of Your wings.

units.leftText: My soul stays close to you. Your right hand holds me up.
units.rightText: My soul clings to You; Your right hand upholds me.

units.leftText: But those who seek my soul to destroy it shall go into the lower parts of the earth.
units.rightText: But those who seek my life to destroy it will go into the depths of the earth.

units.leftText: They shall be given over to the power of the sword. They shall be jackal food.
units.rightText: They will fall to the power of the sword; they will become a portion for foxes.

units.leftText: But the king shall rejoice in God. Everyone who swears by him will praise him, for the mouth of those who speak lies shall be silenced.
units.rightText: But the king will rejoice in God; all who swear by Him will exult, for the mouths of liars will be shut.

units.leftText: Hear my voice, God, in my complaint. Preserve my life from fear of the enemy.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. Hear, O God, my voice of complaint; preserve my life from dread of the enemy.

units.leftText: Hide me from the conspiracy of the wicked, from the noisy crowd of the ones doing evil;
units.rightText: Hide me from the scheming of the wicked, from the mob of workers of iniquity,

units.leftText: who sharpen their tongue like a sword, and aim their arrows, deadly words,
units.rightText: who sharpen their tongues like swords and aim their bitter words like arrows,

units.leftText: to shoot innocent men from ambushes. They shoot at him suddenly and fearlessly.
units.rightText: ambushing the innocent in seclusion, shooting suddenly, without fear.

units.leftText: They encourage themselves in evil plans. They talk about laying snares secretly. They say, “Who will see them?”
units.rightText: They hold fast to their evil purpose; they speak of hiding their snares. “Who will see them?” they say.

units.leftText: They plot injustice, saying, “We have made a perfect plan!” Surely man’s mind and heart are cunning.
units.rightText: They devise injustice and say, “We have perfected a secret plan.” For the inner man and the heart are mysterious.

units.leftText: But God will shoot at them. They will be suddenly struck down with an arrow.
units.rightText: But God will shoot them with arrows; suddenly they will be wounded.

units.leftText: Their own tongues shall ruin them. All who see them will shake their heads.
units.rightText: They will be made to stumble, their own tongues turned against them. All who see will shake their heads.

units.leftText: All mankind shall be afraid. They shall declare the work of God, and shall wisely ponder what he has done.
units.rightText: Then all mankind will fear and proclaim the work of God; so they will ponder what He has done.

units.leftText: The righteous shall be glad in the LORD, and shall take refuge in him. All the upright in heart shall praise him!
units.rightText: Let the righteous rejoice in the LORD and take refuge in Him; let all the upright in heart exult.

units.leftText: Praise waits for you, God, in Zion. Vows shall be performed to you.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. A song. Praise awaits You, O God, in Zion; to You our vows will be fulfilled.

units.leftText: You who hear prayer, all men will come to you.
units.rightText: O You who listen to prayer, all people will come to You.

units.leftText: Sins overwhelmed me, but you atoned for our transgressions.
units.rightText: When iniquities prevail against me, You atone for our transgressions.

units.leftText: Blessed is the one whom you choose and cause to come near, that he may live in your courts. We will be filled with the goodness of your house, your holy temple.
units.rightText: Blessed is the one You choose and bring near to dwell in Your courts! We are filled with the goodness of Your house, the holiness of Your temple.

units.leftText: By awesome deeds of righteousness, you answer us, God of our salvation. You who are the hope of all the ends of the earth, of those who are far away on the sea.
units.rightText: With awesome deeds of righteousness You answer us, O God of our salvation, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of the farthest seas.

units.leftText: By your power, you form the mountains, having armed yourself with strength.
units.rightText: You formed the mountains by Your power, having girded Yourself with might.

units.leftText: You still the roaring of the seas, the roaring of their waves, and the turmoil of the nations.
units.rightText: You stilled the roaring of the seas, the pounding of their waves, and the tumult of the nations.

units.leftText: They also who dwell in faraway places are afraid at your wonders. You call the morning’s dawn and the evening with songs of joy.
units.rightText: Those who live far away fear Your wonders; You make the dawn and sunset shout for joy.
rightNotes: 65:8 Or where morning dawns and evening fades You call forth songs of joy.

units.leftText: You visit the earth, and water it. You greatly enrich it. The river of God is full of water. You provide them grain, for so you have ordained it.
units.rightText: You attend to the earth and water it; with abundance You enrich it. The streams of God are full of water, for You prepare our grain by providing for the earth.
rightNotes: 65:9 Or and make it overflow
65:9 Or to provide the people with grain, for so You have ordained it

units.leftText: You drench its furrows. You level its ridges. You soften it with showers. You bless it with a crop.
units.rightText: You soak its furrows and level its ridges; You soften it with showers and bless its growth.

units.leftText: You crown the year with your bounty. Your carts overflow with abundance.
units.rightText: You crown the year with Your bounty, and Your paths overflow with plenty.

units.leftText: The wilderness grasslands overflow. The hills are clothed with gladness.
units.rightText: The pastures of the wilderness overflow; the hills are robed with joy.

units.leftText: The pastures are covered with flocks. The valleys also are clothed with grain. They shout for joy! They also sing.
units.rightText: The pastures are clothed with flocks, and the valleys are decked with grain. They shout in triumph; indeed, they sing.

units.leftText: Make a joyful shout to God, all the earth!
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. A song. A Psalm. Make a joyful noise to God, all the earth!

units.leftText: Sing to the glory of his name! Offer glory and praise!
units.rightText: Sing the glory of His name; make His praise glorious.

units.leftText: Tell God, “How awesome are your deeds! Through the greatness of your power, your enemies submit themselves to you.
units.rightText: Say to God, “How awesome are Your deeds! So great is Your power that Your enemies cower before You.

units.leftText: All the earth will worship you, and will sing to you; they will sing to your name.” Selah.*
units.rightText: All the earth bows down to You; they sing praise to You; they sing praise to Your name.” Selah

units.leftText: Come, and see God’s deeds— awesome work on behalf of the children of men.
units.rightText: Come and see the works of God; how awesome are His deeds toward mankind.

units.leftText: He turned the sea into dry land. They went through the river on foot. There, we rejoiced in him.
units.rightText: He turned the sea into dry land; they passed through the waters on foot; there we rejoiced in Him.

units.leftText: He rules by his might forever. His eyes watch the nations. Don’t let the rebellious rise up against him. Selah.*
units.rightText: He rules forever by His power; His eyes watch the nations. Do not let the rebellious exalt themselves. Selah

units.leftText: Praise our God, you peoples! Make the sound of his praise heard,
units.rightText: Bless our God, O peoples; let the sound of His praise be heard.

units.leftText: who preserves our life among the living, and doesn’t allow our feet to be moved.
units.rightText: He preserves our lives and keeps our feet from slipping.

units.leftText: For you, God, have tested us. You have refined us, as silver is refined.
units.rightText: For You , O God, have tested us; You have refined us like silver.

units.leftText: You brought us into prison. You laid a burden on our backs.
units.rightText: You led us into the net; You laid burdens on our backs.

units.leftText: You allowed men to ride over our heads. We went through fire and through water, but you brought us to the place of abundance.
units.rightText: You let men ride over our heads; we went through fire and water, but You brought us into abundance.

units.leftText: I will come into your temple with burnt offerings. I will pay my vows to you,
units.rightText: I will enter Your house with burnt offerings; I will fulfill my vows to You —

units.leftText: which my lips promised, and my mouth spoke, when I was in distress.
units.rightText: the vows that my lips promised and my mouth spoke in my distress.

units.leftText: I will offer to you burnt offerings of fat animals, with the offering of rams, I will offer bulls with goats. Selah.*
units.rightText: I will offer You fatlings as burnt offerings, with the fragrant smoke of rams; I will offer bulls and goats. Selah

units.leftText: Come and hear, all you who fear God. I will declare what he has done for my soul.
units.rightText: Come and listen, all you who fear God, and I will declare what He has done for me.

units.leftText: I cried to him with my mouth. He was extolled with my tongue.
units.rightText: I cried out to Him with my mouth and praised Him with my tongue.
rightNotes: 66:17 Or and His praise was on my tongue

units.leftText: If I cherished sin in my heart, the Lord wouldn’t have listened.
units.rightText: If I had cherished iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.

units.leftText: But most certainly, God has listened. He has heard the voice of my prayer.
units.rightText: But God has surely heard; He has attended to the sound of my prayer.

units.leftText: Blessed be God, who has not turned away my prayer, nor his loving kindness from me.
units.rightText: Blessed be God, who has not rejected my prayer or withheld from me His loving devotion!

units.leftText: May God be merciful to us, bless us, and cause his face to shine on us. Selah.*
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Psalm. A song. May God be gracious to us and bless us, and cause His face to shine upon us, Selah

units.leftText: That your way may be known on earth, and your salvation among all nations,
units.rightText: that Your ways may be known on earth, Your salvation among all nations.

units.leftText: let the peoples praise you, God. Let all the peoples praise you.
units.rightText: Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You.

units.leftText: Oh let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for you will judge the peoples with equity, and govern the nations on earth. Selah.*
units.rightText: Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for You judge the peoples justly and lead the nations of the earth. Selah

units.leftText: Let the peoples praise you, God. Let all the peoples praise you.
units.rightText: Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You.

units.leftText: The earth has yielded its increase. God, even our own God, will bless us.
units.rightText: The earth has yielded its harvest; God, our God, blesses us.

units.leftText: God will bless us. All the ends of the earth shall fear him.
units.rightText: God blesses us, that all the ends of the earth shall fear Him.

units.leftText: Let God arise! Let his enemies be scattered! Let them who hate him also flee before him.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. A song. God arises. His enemies are scattered, and those who hate Him flee His presence.

units.leftText: As smoke is driven away, so drive them away. As wax melts before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.
units.rightText: As smoke is blown away, You will drive them out; as wax melts before the fire, the wicked will perish in the presence of God.

units.leftText: But let the righteous be glad. Let them rejoice before God. Yes, let them rejoice with gladness.
units.rightText: But the righteous will be glad and rejoice before God; they will celebrate with joy.

units.leftText: Sing to God! Sing praises to his name! Extol him who rides on the clouds: to the LORD, his name! Rejoice before him!
units.rightText: Sing to God! Sing praises to His name. Exalt Him who rides on the clouds — His name is the LORD— and rejoice before Him.
leftNotes: 68:4 Hebrew: יה Yah
rightNotes: 68:4 Or rides through the deserts

units.leftText: A father of the fatherless, and a defender of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.
units.rightText: A father of the fatherless and a defender of widows is God in His holy habitation.

units.leftText: God sets the lonely in families. He brings out the prisoners with singing, but the rebellious dwell in a sun-scorched land.
units.rightText: God settles the lonely in families; He leads the prisoners out to prosperity, but the rebellious dwell in a sun-scorched land.

units.leftText: God, when you went out before your people, when you marched through the wilderness... Selah.*
units.rightText: O God, when You went out before Your people, when You marched through the wasteland, Selah

units.leftText: The earth trembled. The sky also poured down rain at the presence of the God of Sinai— at the presence of God, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: the earth shook and the heavens poured down rain before God, the One on Sinai, before God, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: You, God, sent a plentiful rain. You confirmed your inheritance when it was weary.
units.rightText: You sent abundant rain, O God; You refreshed Your weary inheritance.

units.leftText: Your congregation lived therein. You, God, prepared your goodness for the poor.
units.rightText: Your flock settled therein; O God, from Your bounty You provided for the poor.

units.leftText: The Lord announced the word. The ones who proclaim it are a great company.
units.rightText: The Lord gives the command; a great company of women proclaim it:

units.leftText: “Kings of armies flee! They flee!” She who waits at home divides the plunder,
units.rightText: “Kings and their armies flee in haste; she who waits at home divides the plunder.

units.leftText: while you sleep among the camp fires, the wings of a dove sheathed with silver, her feathers with shining gold.
units.rightText: Though you lie down among the sheepfolds, the wings of the dove are covered with silver, and her feathers with shimmering gold.”

units.leftText: When the Almighty scattered kings in her, it snowed on Zalmon.
units.rightText: When the Almighty scattered the kings in the land, it was like the snow falling on Zalmon.
rightNotes: 68:14 Hebrew Shaddai

units.leftText: The mountains of Bashan are majestic mountains. The mountains of Bashan are rugged.
units.rightText: A mountain of God is Mount Bashan; a mountain of many peaks is Mount Bashan.

units.leftText: Why do you look in envy, you rugged mountains, at the mountain where God chooses to reign? Yes, the LORD will dwell there forever.
units.rightText: Why do you gaze in envy, O mountains of many peaks? This is the mountain God chose for His dwelling, where the LORD will surely dwell forever.
leftNotes: 68:16 LORD or GOD in all caps is from the Hebrew יהוה Yahweh except when otherwise noted as being from the short form יה Yah.

units.leftText: The chariots of God are tens of thousands and thousands of thousands. The Lord is among them, from Sinai, into the sanctuary.
units.rightText: The chariots of God are tens of thousands — thousands of thousands are they; the Lord is in His sanctuary as He was at Sinai.
rightNotes: 68:17 Or the Lord has come from Sinai in His holiness

units.leftText: You have ascended on high. You have led away captives. You have received gifts among people, yes, among the rebellious also, that the LORD God might dwell there.
units.rightText: You have ascended on high; You have led captives away. You have received gifts from men, even from the rebellious, that the LORD God may dwell there.
leftNotes: 68:18 Hebrew: יה Yah
rightNotes: 68:18 Cited in Ephesians 4:8|EPH 4:8*

units.leftText: Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears our burdens, even the God who is our salvation. Selah.*
units.rightText: Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears our burden, the God of our salvation. Selah

units.leftText: God is to us a God of deliverance. To GOD, the Lord, belongs escape from death.
units.rightText: Our God is a God of deliverance; the Lord GOD is our rescuer from death.
leftNotes: 68:20 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: But God will strike through the head of his enemies, the hairy scalp of such a one as still continues in his guiltiness.
units.rightText: Surely God will crush the heads of His enemies, the hairy crowns of those who persist in guilty ways.

units.leftText: The Lord said, “I will bring you again from Bashan, I will bring you again from the depths of the sea,
units.rightText: The Lord said, “I will retrieve them from Bashan, I will bring them up from the depths of the sea,

units.leftText: that you may crush them, dipping your foot in blood, that the tongues of your dogs may have their portion from your enemies.”
units.rightText: that your foot may be dipped in the blood of your foes— the tongues of your dogs in the same.”

units.leftText: They have seen your processions, God, even the processions of my God, my King, into the sanctuary.
units.rightText: They have seen Your procession, O God — the march of my God and King into the sanctuary.

units.leftText: The singers went before, the minstrels followed after, among the ladies playing with tambourines,
units.rightText: The singers lead the way, the musicians follow after, among the maidens playing tambourines.

units.leftText: “Bless God in the congregations, even the Lord in the assembly of Israel!”
units.rightText: Bless God in the great congregation; bless the LORD from the fountain of Israel.

units.leftText: There is little Benjamin, their ruler, the princes of Judah, their council, the princes of Zebulun, and the princes of Naphtali.
units.rightText: There is Benjamin, the youngest, ruling them, the princes of Judah in their company, the princes of Zebulun and of Naphtali.

units.leftText: Your God has commanded your strength. Strengthen, God, that which you have done for us.
units.rightText: Summon Your power, O God; show Your strength, O God, which You have exerted on our behalf.
rightNotes: 68:28 LXX and Syriac; most Hebrew manuscripts Your God has summoned your power

units.leftText: Because of your temple at Jerusalem, kings will bring presents to you.
units.rightText: Because of Your temple at Jerusalem kings will bring You gifts.

units.leftText: Rebuke the wild animal of the reeds, the multitude of the bulls with the calves of the peoples. Trample under foot the bars of silver. Scatter the nations who delight in war.
units.rightText: Rebuke the beast in the reeds, the herd of bulls among the calves of the nations, until it submits, bringing bars of silver. Scatter the nations who delight in war.

units.leftText: Princes shall come out of Egypt. Ethiopia shall hurry to stretch out her hands to God.
units.rightText: Envoys will arrive from Egypt; Cush will stretch out her hands to God.
rightNotes: 68:31 That is, the upper Nile region

units.leftText: Sing to God, you kingdoms of the earth! Sing praises to the Lord—Selah—*
units.rightText: Sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth; sing praises to the Lord— Selah

units.leftText: to him who rides on the heaven of heavens, which are of old; behold, he utters his voice, a mighty voice.
units.rightText: to Him who rides upon the highest heavens of old; behold, His mighty voice resounds.

units.leftText: Ascribe strength to God! His excellency is over Israel, his strength is in the skies.
units.rightText: Ascribe the power to God, whose majesty is over Israel, whose strength is in the skies.

units.leftText: You are awesome, God, in your sanctuaries. The God of Israel gives strength and power to his people. Praise be to God!
units.rightText: O God, You are awesome in Your sanctuary; the God of Israel Himself gives strength and power to His people. Blessed be God!

units.leftText: Save me, God, for the waters have come up to my neck!
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Lilies.” Of David. Save me, O God, for the waters are up to my neck.

units.leftText: I sink in deep mire, where there is no foothold. I have come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me.
units.rightText: I have sunk into the miry depths, where there is no footing; I have drifted into deep waters, where the flood engulfs me.

units.leftText: I am weary with my crying. My throat is dry. My eyes fail looking for my God.
units.rightText: I am weary from my crying; my throat is parched. My eyes fail, looking for my God.

units.leftText: Those who hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head. Those who want to cut me off, being my enemies wrongfully, are mighty. I have to restore what I didn’t take away.
units.rightText: Those who hate me without cause outnumber the hairs of my head; many are those who would destroy me — my enemies for no reason. Though I did not steal, I must repay.

units.leftText: God, you know my foolishness. My sins aren’t hidden from you.
units.rightText: You know my folly, O God, and my guilt is not hidden from You.

units.leftText: Don’t let those who wait for you be shamed through me, Lord GOD of Armies. Don’t let those who seek you be brought to dishonor through me, God of Israel.
units.rightText: May those who hope in You not be ashamed through me, O Lord GOD of Hosts; may those who seek You not be dishonored through me, O God of Israel.

units.leftText: Because for your sake, I have borne reproach. Shame has covered my face.
units.rightText: For I have endured scorn for Your sake, and shame has covered my face.

units.leftText: I have become a stranger to my brothers, an alien to my mother’s children.
units.rightText: I have become a stranger to my brothers and a foreigner to my mother’s sons,

units.leftText: For the zeal of your house consumes me. The reproaches of those who reproach you have fallen on me.
units.rightText: because zeal for Your house has consumed me, and the insults of those who insult You have fallen on me.
rightNotes: 69:9 Cited in John 2:17|JHN 2:17*
69:9 Cited in Romans 15:3|ROM 15:3*

units.leftText: When I wept and I fasted, that was to my reproach.
units.rightText: I wept and fasted, but it brought me reproach.

units.leftText: When I made sackcloth my clothing, I became a byword to them.
units.rightText: I made sackcloth my clothing, and I was sport to them.

units.leftText: Those who sit in the gate talk about me. I am the song of the drunkards.
units.rightText: Those who sit at the gate mock me, and I am the song of drunkards.

units.leftText: But as for me, my prayer is to you, LORD, in an acceptable time. God, in the abundance of your loving kindness, answer me in the truth of your salvation.
units.rightText: But my prayer to You, O LORD, is for a time of favor. In Your abundant loving devotion, O God, answer me with Your sure salvation.

units.leftText: Deliver me out of the mire, and don’t let me sink. Let me be delivered from those who hate me, and out of the deep waters.
units.rightText: Rescue me from the mire and do not let me sink; deliver me from my foes and out of the deep waters.

units.leftText: Don’t let the flood waters overwhelm me, neither let the deep swallow me up. Don’t let the pit shut its mouth on me.
units.rightText: Do not let the floods engulf me or the depths swallow me up; let not the Pit close its mouth over me.

units.leftText: Answer me, LORD, for your loving kindness is good. According to the multitude of your tender mercies, turn to me.
units.rightText: Answer me, O LORD, for Your loving devotion is good; turn to me in keeping with Your great compassion.

units.leftText: Don’t hide your face from your servant, for I am in distress. Answer me speedily!
units.rightText: Hide not Your face from Your servant, for I am in distress. Answer me quickly!

units.leftText: Draw near to my soul and redeem it. Ransom me because of my enemies.
units.rightText: Draw near to my soul and redeem me; ransom me because of my foes.

units.leftText: You know my reproach, my shame, and my dishonor. My adversaries are all before you.
units.rightText: You know my reproach, my shame and disgrace. All my adversaries are before You.

units.leftText: Reproach has broken my heart, and I am full of heaviness. I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; for comforters, but I found none.
units.rightText: Insults have broken my heart, and I am in despair. I looked for sympathy, but there was none, for comforters, but I found no one.

units.leftText: They also gave me poison for my food. In my thirst, they gave me vinegar to drink.
units.rightText: They poisoned my food with gall and gave me vinegar to quench my thirst.

units.leftText: Let their table before them become a snare. May it become a retribution and a trap.
units.rightText: May their table become a snare; may it be a retribution and a trap.
rightNotes: 69:22 A slight revocalization of the Hebrew (see also LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate); literally may their prosperity be a trap; cited in Romans 11:9|ROM 11:9*

units.leftText: Let their eyes be darkened, so that they can’t see. Let their backs be continually bent.
units.rightText: May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.
rightNotes: 69:23 LXX; Hebrew and may their loins tremble continually; cited in Romans 11:10|ROM 11:10*

units.leftText: Pour out your indignation on them. Let the fierceness of your anger overtake them.
units.rightText: Pour out Your wrath upon them, and let Your burning anger overtake them.

units.leftText: Let their habitation be desolate. Let no one dwell in their tents.
units.rightText: May their place be deserted; let there be no one to dwell in their tents.
rightNotes: 69:25 Cited in Acts 1:20|ACT 1:20*

units.leftText: For they persecute him whom you have wounded. They tell of the sorrow of those whom you have hurt.
units.rightText: For they persecute the one You struck and recount the pain of those You wounded.

units.leftText: Charge them with crime upon crime. Don’t let them come into your righteousness.
units.rightText: Add iniquity to their iniquity; let them not share in Your righteousness.

units.leftText: Let them be blotted out of the book of life, and not be written with the righteous.
units.rightText: May they be blotted out of the Book of Life and not listed with the righteous.

units.leftText: But I am in pain and distress. Let your salvation, God, protect me.
units.rightText: But I am in pain and distress; let Your salvation protect me, O God.

units.leftText: I will praise the name of God with a song, and will magnify him with thanksgiving.
units.rightText: I will praise God’s name in song and exalt Him with thanksgiving.

units.leftText: It will please the LORD better than an ox, or a bull that has horns and hoofs.
units.rightText: And this will please the LORD more than an ox, more than a bull with horns and hooves.

units.leftText: The humble have seen it, and are glad. You who seek after God, let your heart live.
units.rightText: The humble will see and rejoice. You who seek God, let your hearts be revived!

units.leftText: For the LORD hears the needy, and doesn’t despise his captive people.
units.rightText: For the LORD listens to the needy and does not despise His captive people.

units.leftText: Let heaven and earth praise him; the seas, and everything that moves therein!
units.rightText: Let heaven and earth praise Him, the seas and everything that moves in them.

units.leftText: For God will save Zion, and build the cities of Judah. They shall settle there, and own it.
units.rightText: For God will save Zion and rebuild the cities of Judah, that they may dwell there and possess it.

units.leftText: The children also of his servants shall inherit it. Those who love his name shall dwell therein.
units.rightText: The descendants of His servants will inherit it, and those who love His name will settle in it.

units.leftText: Hurry, God, to deliver me. Come quickly to help me, LORD.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. Of David. To bring remembrance. Make haste, O God, to deliver me! Hurry, O LORD, to help me!
