units.leftText: Let them be disappointed and confounded who seek my soul. Let those who desire my ruin be turned back in disgrace.
units.rightText: May those who seek my life be ashamed and confounded; may those who wish me harm be repelled and humiliated.

units.leftText: Let them be turned because of their shame who say, “Aha! Aha!”
units.rightText: May those who say, “Aha, aha!” retreat because of their shame.

units.leftText: Let all those who seek you rejoice and be glad in you. Let those who love your salvation continually say, “Let God be exalted!”
units.rightText: May all who seek You rejoice and be glad in You; may those who love Your salvation always say, “Let God be magnified!”

units.leftText: But I am poor and needy. Come to me quickly, God. You are my help and my deliverer. LORD, don’t delay.
units.rightText: But I am poor and needy; hurry to me, O God. You are my help and my deliverer; O LORD, do not delay.

units.leftText: In you, LORD, I take refuge. Never let me be disappointed.
units.rightText: In You, O LORD, I have taken refuge; let me never be put to shame.

units.leftText: Deliver me in your righteousness, and rescue me. Turn your ear to me, and save me.
units.rightText: In Your justice, rescue and deliver me; incline Your ear and save me.

units.leftText: Be to me a rock of refuge to which I may always go. Give the command to save me, for you are my rock and my fortress.
units.rightText: Be my rock of refuge, where I can always go. Give the command to save me, for You are my rock and my fortress.

units.leftText: Rescue me, my God, from the hand of the wicked, from the hand of the unrighteous and cruel man.
units.rightText: Deliver me, O my God, from the hand of the wicked, from the grasp of the unjust and ruthless.

units.leftText: For you are my hope, Lord GOD, my confidence from my youth.
units.rightText: For You are my hope, O Lord GOD, my confidence from my youth.

units.leftText: I have relied on you from the womb. You are he who took me out of my mother’s womb. I will always praise you.
units.rightText: I have leaned on You since birth; You pulled me from my mother’s womb. My praise is always for You.

units.leftText: I am a marvel to many, but you are my strong refuge.
units.rightText: I have become a portent to many, but You are my strong refuge.

units.leftText: My mouth shall be filled with your praise, with your honor all day long.
units.rightText: My mouth is filled with Your praise and with Your splendor all day long.

units.leftText: Don’t reject me in my old age. Don’t forsake me when my strength fails.
units.rightText: Do not discard me in my old age; do not forsake me when my strength fails.

units.leftText: For my enemies talk about me. Those who watch for my soul conspire together,
units.rightText: For my enemies speak against me, and those who lie in wait for my life conspire,

units.leftText: saying, “God has forsaken him. Pursue and take him, for no one will rescue him.”
units.rightText: saying, “God has forsaken him; pursue him and seize him, for there is no one to rescue him.”

units.leftText: God, don’t be far from me. My God, hurry to help me.
units.rightText: Be not far from me, O God. Hurry, O my God, to help me.

units.leftText: Let my accusers be disappointed and consumed. Let them be covered with disgrace and scorn who want to harm me.
units.rightText: May the accusers of my soul be ashamed and consumed; may those who seek my harm be covered with scorn and disgrace.

units.leftText: But I will always hope, and will add to all of your praise.
units.rightText: But I will always hope and will praise You more and more.

units.leftText: My mouth will tell about your righteousness, and of your salvation all day, though I don’t know its full measure.
units.rightText: My mouth will declare Your righteousness and Your salvation all day long, though I cannot know their full measure.

units.leftText: I will come with the mighty acts of the Lord GOD. I will make mention of your righteousness, even of yours alone.
units.rightText: I will come in the strength of the Lord GOD; I will proclaim Your righteousness — Yours alone.

units.leftText: God, you have taught me from my youth. Until now, I have declared your wondrous works.
units.rightText: O God, You have taught me from my youth, and to this day I proclaim Your marvelous deeds.

units.leftText: Yes, even when I am old and gray-haired, God, don’t forsake me, until I have declared your strength to the next generation, your might to everyone who is to come.
units.rightText: Even when I am old and gray, do not forsake me, O God, until I proclaim Your power to the next generation, Your might to all who are to come.

units.leftText: God, your righteousness also reaches to the heavens. You have done great things. God, who is like you?
units.rightText: Your righteousness reaches to the heavens, O God, You who have done great things. Who, O God, is like You?

units.leftText: You, who have shown us many and bitter troubles, you will let me live. You will bring us up again from the depths of the earth.
units.rightText: Though You have shown me many troubles and misfortunes, You will revive me once again. Even from the depths of the earth You will bring me back up.

units.leftText: Increase my honor and comfort me again.
units.rightText: You will increase my honor and comfort me once again.

units.leftText: I will also praise you with the harp for your faithfulness, my God. I sing praises to you with the lyre, Holy One of Israel.
units.rightText: So I will praise You with the harp for Your faithfulness, O my God; I will sing praise to You with the lyre, O Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: My lips shall shout for joy! My soul, which you have redeemed, sings praises to you!
units.rightText: When I sing praise to You my lips will shout for joy, along with my soul, which You have redeemed.

units.leftText: My tongue will also talk about your righteousness all day long, for they are disappointed, and they are confounded, who want to harm me.
units.rightText: My tongue will indeed proclaim Your righteousness all day long, for those who seek my harm are disgraced and confounded.

units.leftText: God, give the king your justice; your righteousness to the royal son.
units.rightText: Of Solomon. Endow the king with Your justice, O God, and the son of the king with Your righteousness.

units.leftText: He will judge your people with righteousness, and your poor with justice.
units.rightText: May he judge Your people with righteousness and Your afflicted with justice.

units.leftText: The mountains shall bring prosperity to the people. The hills bring the fruit of righteousness.
units.rightText: May the mountains bring peace to the people, and the hills bring righteousness.

units.leftText: He will judge the poor of the people. He will save the children of the needy, and will break the oppressor in pieces.
units.rightText: May he vindicate the afflicted among the people; may he save the children of the needy and crush the oppressor.

units.leftText: They shall fear you while the sun endures; and as long as the moon, throughout all generations.
units.rightText: May they fear him as long as the sun shines, as long as the moon remains, through all generations.
rightNotes: 72:5 LXX He shall endure

units.leftText: He will come down like rain on the mown grass, as showers that water the earth.
units.rightText: May he be like rain that falls on freshly cut grass, like spring showers that water the earth.

units.leftText: In his days, the righteous shall flourish, and abundance of peace, until the moon is no more.
units.rightText: May the righteous flourish in his days and prosperity abound until the moon is no more.

units.leftText: He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, from the River to the ends of the earth.
units.rightText: May he rule from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth.
rightNotes: 72:8 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: Those who dwell in the wilderness shall bow before him. His enemies shall lick the dust.
units.rightText: May the nomads bow before him, and his enemies lick the dust.

units.leftText: The kings of Tarshish and of the islands will bring tribute. The kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts.
units.rightText: May the kings of Tarshish and distant shores bring tribute; may the kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts.

units.leftText: Yes, all kings shall fall down before him. All nations shall serve him.
units.rightText: May all kings bow down to him and all nations serve him.

units.leftText: For he will deliver the needy when he cries; the poor, who has no helper.
units.rightText: For he will deliver the needy who cry out and the afflicted who have no helper.

units.leftText: He will have pity on the poor and needy. He will save the souls of the needy.
units.rightText: He will take pity on the poor and needy and save the lives of the oppressed.

units.leftText: He will redeem their soul from oppression and violence. Their blood will be precious in his sight.
units.rightText: He will redeem them from oppression and violence, for their blood is precious in his sight.

units.leftText: He will live; and Sheba’s gold will be given to him. Men will pray for him continually. They will bless him all day long.
units.rightText: Long may he live! May gold from Sheba be given him. May people ever pray for him; may they bless him all day long.

units.leftText: Abundance of grain shall be throughout the land. Its fruit sways like Lebanon. Let it flourish, thriving like the grass of the field.
units.rightText: May there be an abundance of grain in the land; may it sway atop the hills. May its fruit trees flourish like the forests of Lebanon, the people of its cities like the grass of the field.

units.leftText: His name endures forever. His name continues as long as the sun. Men shall be blessed by him. All nations will call him blessed.
units.rightText: May his name endure forever; may his name continue as long as the sun shines. In him may all nations be blessed; may they call him blessed.
rightNotes: 72:17 Or increase

units.leftText: Praise be to the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does marvelous deeds.
units.rightText: Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does marvelous deeds.

units.leftText: Blessed be his glorious name forever! Let the whole earth be filled with his glory! Amen and amen.
units.rightText: And blessed be His glorious name forever; may all the earth be filled with His glory. Amen and amen.

units.leftText: This ends the prayers by David, the son of Jesse.
units.rightText: Thus conclude the prayers of David son of Jesse.

units.leftText: Surely God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart.
units.rightText: A Psalm of Asaph. Surely God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart.
leftNotes: 73:1 The Hebrew word rendered “God” is “אֱלֹהִ֑ים*” (Elohim).

units.leftText: But as for me, my feet were almost gone. My steps had nearly slipped.
units.rightText: But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled; my steps had nearly slipped.

units.leftText: For I was envious of the arrogant, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
units.rightText: For I envied the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.

units.leftText: For there are no struggles in their death, but their strength is firm.
units.rightText: They have no struggle in their death; their bodies are well-fed.

units.leftText: They are free from burdens of men, neither are they plagued like other men.
units.rightText: They are free of the burdens others carry; they are not afflicted like other men.

units.leftText: Therefore pride is like a chain around their neck. Violence covers them like a garment.
units.rightText: Therefore pride is their necklace; a garment of violence covers them.

units.leftText: Their eyes bulge with fat. Their minds pass the limits of conceit.
units.rightText: From their prosperity proceeds iniquity; the imaginations of their hearts run wild.
rightNotes: 73:7 Literally Their eye bulges with fatness; Syriac From their callous heart proceeds iniquity

units.leftText: They scoff and speak with malice. In arrogance, they threaten oppression.
units.rightText: They mock and speak with malice; with arrogance they threaten oppression.

units.leftText: They have set their mouth in the heavens. Their tongue walks through the earth.
units.rightText: They set their mouths against the heavens, and their tongues strut across the earth.

units.leftText: Therefore their people return to them, and they drink up waters of abundance.
units.rightText: So their people return to this place and drink up waters in abundance.
rightNotes: 73:10 Or His people

units.leftText: They say, “How does God know? Is there knowledge in the Most High?”
units.rightText: The wicked say, “How can God know? Does the Most High have knowledge?”

units.leftText: Behold, these are the wicked. Being always at ease, they increase in riches.
units.rightText: Behold, these are the wicked — always carefree as they increase their wealth.

units.leftText: Surely I have cleansed my heart in vain, and washed my hands in innocence,
units.rightText: Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure; in innocence I have washed my hands.

units.leftText: For all day long I have been plagued, and punished every morning.
units.rightText: For I am afflicted all day long and punished every morning.

units.leftText: If I had said, “I will speak thus”, behold, I would have betrayed the generation of your children.
units.rightText: If I had said, “I will speak this way,” then I would have betrayed Your children.

units.leftText: When I tried to understand this, it was too painful for me—
units.rightText: When I tried to understand all this, it was troublesome in my sight

units.leftText: until I entered God’s sanctuary, and considered their latter end.
units.rightText: until I entered God’s sanctuary; then I discerned their end.

units.leftText: Surely you set them in slippery places. You throw them down to destruction.
units.rightText: Surely You set them on slick ground; You cast them down into ruin.

units.leftText: How they are suddenly destroyed! They are completely swept away with terrors.
units.rightText: How suddenly they are laid waste, completely swept away by terrors!

units.leftText: As a dream when one wakes up, so, Lord, when you awake, you will despise their fantasies.
units.rightText: Like one waking from a dream, so You, O Lord, awaken and despise their form.
leftNotes: 73:20 The word translated “Lord” is “Adonai.”

units.leftText: For my soul was grieved. I was embittered in my heart.
units.rightText: When my heart was grieved and I was pierced within,

units.leftText: I was so senseless and ignorant. I was a brute beast before you.
units.rightText: I was senseless and ignorant; I was a brute beast before You.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, I am continually with you. You have held my right hand.
units.rightText: Yet I am always with You; You hold my right hand.

units.leftText: You will guide me with your counsel, and afterward receive me to glory.
units.rightText: You guide me with Your counsel, and later receive me in glory.

units.leftText: Whom do I have in heaven? There is no one on earth whom I desire besides you.
units.rightText: Whom have I in heaven but You? And on earth I desire no one besides You.

units.leftText: My flesh and my heart fails, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
units.rightText: My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
rightNotes: 73:26 Hebrew rock

units.leftText: For, behold, those who are far from you shall perish. You have destroyed all those who are unfaithful to you.
units.rightText: Those far from You will surely perish; You destroy all who are unfaithful to You.

units.leftText: But it is good for me to come close to God. I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may tell of all your works.
units.rightText: But as for me, it is good to draw near to God. I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may proclaim all Your works.
leftNotes: 73:28 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: God, why have you rejected us forever? Why does your anger smolder against the sheep of your pasture?
units.rightText: A Maskil of Asaph. Why have You rejected us forever, O God? Why does Your anger smolder against the sheep of Your pasture?
rightNotes: 74:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142.

units.leftText: Remember your congregation, which you purchased of old, which you have redeemed to be the tribe of your inheritance: Mount Zion, in which you have lived.
units.rightText: Remember Your congregation, which You purchased long ago and redeemed as the tribe of Your inheritance — Mount Zion, where You dwell.

units.leftText: Lift up your feet to the perpetual ruins, all the evil that the enemy has done in the sanctuary.
units.rightText: Turn Your steps to the everlasting ruins, to everything in the sanctuary the enemy has destroyed.

units.leftText: Your adversaries have roared in the middle of your assembly. They have set up their standards as signs.
units.rightText: Your foes have roared within Your meeting place; they have unfurled their banners as signs,

units.leftText: They behaved like men wielding axes, cutting through a thicket of trees.
units.rightText: like men wielding axes in a thicket of trees

units.leftText: Now they break all its carved work down with hatchet and hammers.
units.rightText: and smashing all the carvings with hatchets and picks.

units.leftText: They have burned your sanctuary to the ground. They have profaned the dwelling place of your Name.
units.rightText: They have burned Your sanctuary to the ground; they have defiled the dwelling place of Your Name.

units.leftText: They said in their heart, “We will crush them completely.” They have burned up all the places in the land where God was worshiped.
units.rightText: They said in their hearts, “We will crush them completely.” They burned down every place where God met us in the land.

units.leftText: We see no miraculous signs. There is no longer any prophet, neither is there among us anyone who knows how long.
units.rightText: There are no signs for us to see. There is no longer any prophet. And none of us knows how long this will last.

units.leftText: How long, God, shall the adversary reproach? Shall the enemy blaspheme your name forever?
units.rightText: How long, O God, will the enemy taunt You? Will the foe revile Your name forever?

units.leftText: Why do you draw back your hand, even your right hand? Take it from your chest and consume them!
units.rightText: Why do You withdraw Your strong right hand? Stretch it out to destroy them!
rightNotes: 74:11 Literally From the midst of Your bosom destroy them! or From the midst of Your bosom remove it!

units.leftText: Yet God is my King of old, working salvation throughout the earth.
units.rightText: Yet God is my King from ancient times, working salvation on the earth.

units.leftText: You divided the sea by your strength. You broke the heads of the sea monsters in the waters.
units.rightText: You divided the sea by Your strength; You smashed the heads of the dragons of the sea;

units.leftText: You broke the heads of Leviathan in pieces. You gave him as food to people and desert creatures.
units.rightText: You crushed the heads of Leviathan; You fed him to the creatures of the desert.

units.leftText: You opened up spring and stream. You dried up mighty rivers.
units.rightText: You broke open the fountain and the flood; You dried up the ever-flowing rivers.

units.leftText: The day is yours, the night is also yours. You have prepared the light and the sun.
units.rightText: The day is Yours, and also the night; You established the moon and the sun.
rightNotes: 74:16 Literally the light

units.leftText: You have set all the boundaries of the earth. You have made summer and winter.
units.rightText: You set all the boundaries of the earth; You made the summer and winter.

units.leftText: Remember this, that the enemy has mocked you, LORD. Foolish people have blasphemed your name.
units.rightText: Remember how the enemy has mocked You, O LORD, how a foolish people has spurned Your name.

units.leftText: Don’t deliver the soul of your dove to wild beasts. Don’t forget the life of your poor forever.
units.rightText: Do not deliver the soul of Your dove to beasts; do not forget the lives of Your afflicted forever.

units.leftText: Honor your covenant, for haunts of violence fill the dark places of the earth.
units.rightText: Consider Your covenant, for haunts of violence fill the dark places of the land.

units.leftText: Don’t let the oppressed return ashamed. Let the poor and needy praise your name.
units.rightText: Do not let the oppressed retreat in shame; may the poor and needy praise Your name.

units.leftText: Arise, God! Plead your own cause. Remember how the foolish man mocks you all day.
units.rightText: Rise up, O God; defend Your cause! Remember how the fool mocks You all day long.

units.leftText: Don’t forget the voice of your adversaries. The tumult of those who rise up against you ascends continually.
units.rightText: Do not disregard the clamor of Your adversaries, the uproar of Your enemies that ascends continually.

units.leftText: We give thanks to you, God. We give thanks, for your Name is near. Men tell about your wondrous works.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster: To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Psalm of Asaph. A song. We give thanks to You, O God; we give thanks, for Your Name is near. The people declare Your wondrous works.

units.leftText: When I choose the appointed time, I will judge blamelessly.
units.rightText: “When I choose a time, I will judge fairly.

units.leftText: The earth and all its inhabitants quake. I firmly hold its pillars. Selah.*
units.rightText: When the earth and all its dwellers quake, it is I who bear up its pillars. Selah

units.leftText: I said to the arrogant, “Don’t boast!” I said to the wicked, “Don’t lift up the horn.
units.rightText: I say to the proud, ‘Do not boast,’ and to the wicked, ‘Do not lift up your horn.

units.leftText: Don’t lift up your horn on high. Don’t speak with a stiff neck.”
units.rightText: Do not lift up your horn against heaven or speak with an outstretched neck.’”

units.leftText: For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor yet from the south, comes exaltation.
units.rightText: For exaltation comes neither from east nor west, nor out of the desert,

units.leftText: But God is the judge. He puts down one, and lifts up another.
units.rightText: but it is God who judges; He brings down one and exalts another.

units.leftText: For in the LORD’s hand there is a cup, full of foaming wine mixed with spices. He pours it out. Indeed the wicked of the earth drink and drink it to its very dregs.
units.rightText: For a cup is in the hand of the LORD, full of foaming wine mixed with spices. He pours from His cup, and all the wicked of the earth drink it down to the dregs.

units.leftText: But I will declare this forever: I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.
units.rightText: But I will proclaim Him forever; I will sing praise to the God of Jacob.
rightNotes: 75:9 Or proclaim it

units.leftText: I will cut off all the horns of the wicked, but the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up.
units.rightText: “All the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous will be exalted.”

units.leftText: In Judah, God is known. His name is great in Israel.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Psalm of Asaph. A song. God is known in Judah; His name is great in Israel.

units.leftText: His tabernacle is also in Salem. His dwelling place in Zion.
units.rightText: His tent is in Salem, His dwelling place in Zion.
rightNotes: 76:2 That is, Jerusalem

units.leftText: There he broke the flaming arrows of the bow, the shield, and the sword, and the weapons of war. Selah.*
units.rightText: There He shattered the flaming arrows, the shield and sword and weapons of war. Selah

units.leftText: Glorious are you, and excellent, more than mountains of game.
units.rightText: You are resplendent with light, more majestic than mountains filled with game.

units.leftText: Valiant men lie plundered, they have slept their last sleep. None of the men of war can lift their hands.
units.rightText: The valiant lie plundered; they sleep their last sleep. No men of might could lift a hand.

units.leftText: At your rebuke, God of Jacob, both chariot and horse are cast into a dead sleep.
units.rightText: At Your rebuke, O God of Jacob, both horse and rider lie stunned.

units.leftText: You, even you, are to be feared. Who can stand in your sight when you are angry?
units.rightText: You alone are to be feared. When You are angry, who can stand before You?

units.leftText: You pronounced judgment from heaven. The earth feared, and was silent,
units.rightText: From heaven You pronounced judgment, and the earth feared and was still

units.leftText: when God arose to judgment, to save all the afflicted ones of the earth. Selah.*
units.rightText: when God rose up to judge, to save all the lowly of the earth. Selah

units.leftText: Surely the wrath of man praises you. The survivors of your wrath are restrained.
units.rightText: Even the wrath of man shall praise You; with the survivors of wrath You will clothe Yourself.
rightNotes: 76:10 Or Surely Your wrath against men brings You praise, and the survivors of Your wrath will be restrained.

units.leftText: Make vows to the LORD your God, and fulfill them! Let all of his neighbors bring presents to him who is to be feared.
units.rightText: Make and fulfill your vows to the LORD your God; let all the neighboring lands bring tribute to Him who is to be feared.

units.leftText: He will cut off the spirit of princes. He is feared by the kings of the earth.
units.rightText: He breaks the spirits of princes; He is feared by the kings of the earth.

units.leftText: My cry goes to God! Indeed, I cry to God for help, and for him to listen to me.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. According to Jeduthun. A Psalm of Asaph. I cried out to God; I cried aloud to God to hear me.

units.leftText: In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord. My hand was stretched out in the night, and didn’t get tired. My soul refused to be comforted.
units.rightText: In the day of trouble I sought the Lord; through the night my outstretched hands did not grow weary; my soul refused to be comforted.

units.leftText: I remember God, and I groan. I complain, and my spirit is overwhelmed. Selah.*
units.rightText: I remembered You, O God, and I groaned; I mused and my spirit grew faint. Selah

units.leftText: You hold my eyelids open. I am so troubled that I can’t speak.
units.rightText: You have kept my eyes from closing; I am too troubled to speak.

units.leftText: I have considered the days of old, the years of ancient times.
units.rightText: I considered the days of old, the years long in the past.

units.leftText: I remember my song in the night. I consider in my own heart; my spirit diligently inquires:
units.rightText: At night I remembered my song; in my heart I mused, and my spirit pondered:

units.leftText: “Will the Lord reject us forever? Will he be favorable no more?
units.rightText: “Will the Lord spurn us forever and never show His favor again?

units.leftText: Has his loving kindness vanished forever? Does his promise fail for generations?
units.rightText: Is His loving devotion gone forever? Has His promise failed for all time?

units.leftText: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has he, in anger, withheld his compassion?” Selah.*
units.rightText: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has His anger shut off His compassion?” Selah

units.leftText: Then I thought, “I will appeal to this: the years of the right hand of the Most High.”
units.rightText: So I said, “I am grieved that the right hand of the Most High has changed.”
rightNotes: 77:10 Or “To this I will appeal: to the years of the right hand of the Most High.”

units.leftText: I will remember the LORD’s deeds; for I will remember your wonders of old.
units.rightText: I will remember the works of the LORD; yes, I will remember Your wonders of old.

units.leftText: I will also meditate on all your work, and consider your doings.
units.rightText: I will reflect on all You have done and ponder Your mighty deeds.

units.leftText: Your way, God, is in the sanctuary. What god is great like God?
units.rightText: Your way, O God, is holy. What god is so great as our God?

units.leftText: You are the God who does wonders. You have made your strength known among the peoples.
units.rightText: You are the God who works wonders; You display Your strength among the peoples.

units.leftText: You have redeemed your people with your arm, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.*
units.rightText: With power You redeemed Your people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah

units.leftText: The waters saw you, God. The waters saw you, and they writhed. The depths also convulsed.
units.rightText: The waters saw You, O God; the waters saw You and swirled; even the depths were shaken.

units.leftText: The clouds poured out water. The skies resounded with thunder. Your arrows also flashed around.
units.rightText: The clouds poured down water; the skies resounded with thunder; Your arrows flashed back and forth.

units.leftText: The voice of your thunder was in the whirlwind. The lightnings lit up the world. The earth trembled and shook.
units.rightText: Your thunder resounded in the whirlwind; the lightning lit up the world; the earth trembled and quaked.

units.leftText: Your way was through the sea, your paths through the great waters. Your footsteps were not known.
units.rightText: Your path led through the sea, Your way through the mighty waters, but Your footprints were not to be found.
rightNotes: 77:19 Or were unknown

units.leftText: You led your people like a flock, by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
units.rightText: You led Your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

units.leftText: Hear my teaching, my people. Turn your ears to the words of my mouth.
units.rightText: A Maskil of Asaph. Give ear, O my people, to my instruction; listen to the words of my mouth.
rightNotes: 78:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142.

units.leftText: I will open my mouth in a parable. I will utter dark sayings of old,
units.rightText: I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the beginning,
rightNotes: 78:2 Or from ancient times; see also LXX; cited in Matthew 13:35|MAT 13:35*

units.leftText: which we have heard and known, and our fathers have told us.
units.rightText: that we have heard and known and our fathers have relayed to us.

units.leftText: We will not hide them from their children, telling to the generation to come the praises of the LORD, his strength, and his wondrous deeds that he has done.
units.rightText: We will not hide them from their children but will declare to the next generation the praises of the LORD and His might and the wonders He has performed.

units.leftText: For he established a covenant in Jacob, and appointed a teaching in Israel, which he commanded our fathers, that they should make them known to their children;
units.rightText: For He established a testimony in Jacob and appointed a law in Israel, which He commanded our fathers to teach to their children,

units.leftText: that the generation to come might know, even the children who should be born; who should arise and tell their children,
units.rightText: that the coming generation would know them— even children yet to be born— to arise and tell their own children

units.leftText: that they might set their hope in God, and not forget God’s deeds, but keep his commandments,
units.rightText: that they should put their confidence in God, not forgetting His works, but keeping His commandments.

units.leftText: and might not be as their fathers— a stubborn and rebellious generation, a generation that didn’t make their hearts loyal, whose spirit was not steadfast with God.
units.rightText: Then they will not be like their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation, whose heart was not loyal, whose spirit was not faithful to God.

units.leftText: The children of Ephraim, being armed and carrying bows, turned back in the day of battle.
units.rightText: The archers of Ephraim turned back on the day of battle.

units.leftText: They didn’t keep God’s covenant, and refused to walk in his law.
units.rightText: They failed to keep God’s covenant and refused to live by His law.

units.leftText: They forgot his doings, his wondrous deeds that he had shown them.
units.rightText: They forgot what He had done, the wonders He had shown them.

units.leftText: He did marvelous things in the sight of their fathers, in the land of Egypt, in the field of Zoan.
units.rightText: He worked wonders before their fathers in the land of Egypt, in the region of Zoan.

units.leftText: He split the sea, and caused them to pass through. He made the waters stand as a heap.
units.rightText: He split the sea and brought them through; He set the waters upright like a wall.

units.leftText: In the daytime he also led them with a cloud, and all night with a light of fire.
units.rightText: He led them with a cloud by day and with a light of fire all night.

units.leftText: He split rocks in the wilderness, and gave them drink abundantly as out of the depths.
units.rightText: He split the rocks in the wilderness and gave them drink as abundant as the seas.

units.leftText: He brought streams also out of the rock, and caused waters to run down like rivers.
units.rightText: He brought streams from the stone and made water flow down like rivers.

units.leftText: Yet they still went on to sin against him, to rebel against the Most High in the desert.
units.rightText: But they continued to sin against Him, rebelling in the desert against the Most High.

units.leftText: They tempted God in their heart by asking food according to their desire.
units.rightText: They willfully tested God by demanding the food they craved.

units.leftText: Yes, they spoke against God. They said, “Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?
units.rightText: They spoke against God, saying, “Can God really prepare a table in the wilderness?

units.leftText: Behold, he struck the rock, so that waters gushed out, and streams overflowed. Can he give bread also? Will he provide meat for his people?”
units.rightText: When He struck the rock, water gushed out and torrents raged. But can He also give bread or supply His people with meat?”

units.leftText: Therefore the LORD heard, and was angry. A fire was kindled against Jacob, anger also went up against Israel,
units.rightText: Therefore the LORD heard and was filled with wrath; so a fire was kindled against Jacob, and His anger flared against Israel,

units.leftText: because they didn’t believe in God, and didn’t trust in his salvation.
units.rightText: because they did not believe God or rely on His salvation.

units.leftText: Yet he commanded the skies above, and opened the doors of heaven.
units.rightText: Yet He commanded the clouds above and opened the doors of the heavens.

units.leftText: He rained down manna on them to eat, and gave them food from the sky.
units.rightText: He rained down manna for them to eat; He gave them grain from heaven.
rightNotes: 78:24 Cited in John 6:31|JHN 6:31*

units.leftText: Man ate the bread of angels. He sent them food to the full.
units.rightText: Man ate the bread of angels; He sent them food in abundance.

units.leftText: He caused the east wind to blow in the sky. By his power he guided the south wind.
units.rightText: He stirred the east wind from the heavens and drove the south wind by His might.

units.leftText: He also rained meat on them as the dust, winged birds as the sand of the seas.
units.rightText: He rained meat on them like dust, and winged birds like the sand of the sea.

units.leftText: He let them fall in the middle of their camp, around their habitations.
units.rightText: He felled them in the midst of their camp, all around their dwellings.

units.leftText: So they ate, and were well filled. He gave them their own desire.
units.rightText: So they ate and were well filled, for He gave them what they craved.

units.leftText: They didn’t turn from their cravings. Their food was yet in their mouths,
units.rightText: Yet before they had filled their desire, with the food still in their mouths,

units.leftText: when the anger of God went up against them, killed some of their strongest, and struck down the young men of Israel.
units.rightText: God’s anger flared against them, and He put to death their strongest and subdued the young men of Israel.

units.leftText: For all this they still sinned, and didn’t believe in his wondrous works.
units.rightText: In spite of all this, they kept on sinning; despite His wonderful works, they did not believe.

units.leftText: Therefore he consumed their days in vanity, and their years in terror.
units.rightText: So He ended their days in futility, and their years in sudden terror.
rightNotes: 78:33 Or in vapor

units.leftText: When he killed them, then they inquired after him. They returned and sought God earnestly.
units.rightText: When He slew them, they would seek Him; they repented and searched for God.

units.leftText: They remembered that God was their rock, the Most High God, their redeemer.
units.rightText: And they remembered that God was their Rock, that God Most High was their Redeemer.
rightNotes: 78:35 Hebrew El-Elyon

units.leftText: But they flattered him with their mouth, and lied to him with their tongue.
units.rightText: But they deceived Him with their mouths, and lied to Him with their tongues.

units.leftText: For their heart was not right with him, neither were they faithful in his covenant.
units.rightText: Their hearts were disloyal to Him, and they were unfaithful to His covenant.

units.leftText: But he, being merciful, forgave iniquity, and didn’t destroy them. Yes, many times he turned his anger away, and didn’t stir up all his wrath.
units.rightText: And yet He was compassionate; He forgave their iniquity and did not destroy them. He often restrained His anger and did not unleash His full wrath.

units.leftText: He remembered that they were but flesh, a wind that passes away, and doesn’t come again.
units.rightText: He remembered that they were but flesh, a passing breeze that does not return.

units.leftText: How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness, and grieved him in the desert!
units.rightText: How often they disobeyed Him in the wilderness and grieved Him in the desert!

units.leftText: They turned again and tempted God, and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
units.rightText: Again and again they tested God and provoked the Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: They didn’t remember his hand, nor the day when he redeemed them from the adversary;
units.rightText: They did not remember His power — the day He redeemed them from the adversary,
rightNotes: 78:42 Or His hand

units.leftText: how he set his signs in Egypt, his wonders in the field of Zoan,
units.rightText: when He performed His signs in Egypt and His wonders in the fields of Zoan.

units.leftText: he turned their rivers into blood, and their streams, so that they could not drink.
units.rightText: He turned their rivers to blood, and from their streams they could not drink.

units.leftText: He sent among them swarms of flies, which devoured them; and frogs, which destroyed them.
units.rightText: He sent swarms of flies that devoured them, and frogs that devastated them.

units.leftText: He also gave their increase to the caterpillar, and their labor to the locust.
units.rightText: He gave their crops to the grasshopper, the fruit of their labor to the locust.

units.leftText: He destroyed their vines with hail, their sycamore fig trees with frost.
units.rightText: He killed their vines with hailstones and their sycamore-figs with sleet.
rightNotes: 78:47 Or frost or driving rain

units.leftText: He also gave over their livestock to the hail, and their flocks to hot thunderbolts.
units.rightText: He abandoned their cattle to the hail and their livestock to bolts of lightning.

units.leftText: He threw on them the fierceness of his anger, wrath, indignation, and trouble, and a band of angels of evil.
units.rightText: He unleashed His fury against them, wrath, indignation, and calamity— a band of destroying angels.

units.leftText: He made a path for his anger. He didn’t spare their soul from death, but gave their life over to the pestilence,
units.rightText: He cleared a path for His anger; He did not spare them from death but delivered their lives to the plague.

units.leftText: and struck all the firstborn in Egypt, the chief of their strength in the tents of Ham.
units.rightText: He struck all the firstborn of Egypt, the virility in the tents of Ham.

units.leftText: But he led out his own people like sheep, and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.
units.rightText: He led out His people like sheep and guided them like a flock in the wilderness.

units.leftText: He led them safely, so that they weren’t afraid, but the sea overwhelmed their enemies.
units.rightText: He led them safely, so they did not fear, but the sea engulfed their enemies.

units.leftText: He brought them to the border of his sanctuary, to this mountain, which his right hand had taken.
units.rightText: He brought them to His holy land, to the mountain His right hand had acquired.

units.leftText: He also drove out the nations before them, allotted them for an inheritance by line, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.
units.rightText: He drove out nations before them and apportioned their inheritance; He settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.

units.leftText: Yet they tempted and rebelled against the Most High God, and didn’t keep his testimonies,
units.rightText: But they tested and disobeyed God Most High, for they did not keep His decrees.

units.leftText: but turned back, and dealt treacherously like their fathers. They were twisted like a deceitful bow.
units.rightText: They turned back and were faithless like their fathers, twisted like a faulty bow.

units.leftText: For they provoked him to anger with their high places, and moved him to jealousy with their engraved images.
units.rightText: They enraged Him with their high places and provoked His jealousy with their idols.

units.leftText: When God heard this, he was angry, and greatly abhorred Israel,
units.rightText: On hearing it, God was furious and rejected Israel completely.

units.leftText: so that he abandoned the tent of Shiloh, the tent which he placed among men,
units.rightText: He abandoned the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent He had pitched among men.

units.leftText: and delivered his strength into captivity, his glory into the adversary’s hand.
units.rightText: He delivered His strength to captivity, and His splendor to the hand of the adversary.

units.leftText: He also gave his people over to the sword, and was angry with his inheritance.
units.rightText: He surrendered His people to the sword because He was enraged by His heritage.

units.leftText: Fire devoured their young men. Their virgins had no wedding song.
units.rightText: Fire consumed His young men, and their maidens were left without wedding songs.

units.leftText: Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows couldn’t weep.
units.rightText: His priests fell by the sword, but their widows could not lament.

units.leftText: Then the Lord awakened as one out of sleep, like a mighty man who shouts by reason of wine.
units.rightText: Then the Lord awoke as from sleep, like a mighty warrior overcome by wine.

units.leftText: He struck his adversaries backward. He put them to a perpetual reproach.
units.rightText: He beat back His foes; He put them to everlasting shame.

units.leftText: Moreover he rejected the tent of Joseph, and didn’t choose the tribe of Ephraim,
units.rightText: He rejected the tent of Joseph and refused the tribe of Ephraim.

units.leftText: But chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion which he loved.
units.rightText: But He chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which He loved.

units.leftText: He built his sanctuary like the heights, like the earth which he has established forever.
units.rightText: He built His sanctuary like the heights, like the earth He has established forever.

units.leftText: He also chose David his servant, and took him from the sheepfolds;
units.rightText: He chose David His servant and took him from the sheepfolds;

units.leftText: from following the ewes that have their young, he brought him to be the shepherd of Jacob, his people, and Israel, his inheritance.
units.rightText: from tending the ewes He brought him to be shepherd of His people Jacob, of Israel His inheritance.

units.leftText: So he was their shepherd according to the integrity of his heart, and guided them by the skillfulness of his hands.
units.rightText: So David shepherded them with integrity of heart and guided them with skillful hands.

units.leftText: God, the nations have come into your inheritance. They have defiled your holy temple. They have laid Jerusalem in heaps.
units.rightText: A Psalm of Asaph. The nations, O God, have invaded Your inheritance; they have defiled Your holy temple and reduced Jerusalem to rubble.

units.leftText: They have given the dead bodies of your servants to be food for the birds of the sky, the flesh of your saints to the animals of the earth.
units.rightText: They have given the corpses of Your servants as food to the birds of the air, the flesh of Your saints to the beasts of the earth.

units.leftText: They have shed their blood like water around Jerusalem. There was no one to bury them.
units.rightText: They have poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem, and there is no one to bury the dead.

units.leftText: We have become a reproach to our neighbors, a scoffing and derision to those who are around us.
units.rightText: We have become a reproach to our neighbors, a scorn and derision to those around us.

units.leftText: How long, LORD? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy burn like fire?
units.rightText: How long, O LORD? Will You be angry forever? Will Your jealousy burn like fire?

units.leftText: Pour out your wrath on the nations that don’t know you, on the kingdoms that don’t call on your name,
units.rightText: Pour out Your wrath on the nations that do not acknowledge You, on the kingdoms that refuse to call on Your name,

units.leftText: for they have devoured Jacob, and destroyed his homeland.
units.rightText: for they have devoured Jacob and devastated his homeland.

units.leftText: Don’t hold the iniquities of our forefathers against us. Let your tender mercies speedily meet us, for we are in desperate need.
units.rightText: Do not hold past sins against us; let Your compassion come quickly, for we are brought low.

units.leftText: Help us, God of our salvation, for the glory of your name. Deliver us, and forgive our sins, for your name’s sake.
units.rightText: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of Your name; deliver us and atone for our sins, for the sake of Your name.

units.leftText: Why should the nations say, “Where is their God?” Let it be known among the nations, before our eyes, that vengeance for your servants’ blood is being poured out.
units.rightText: Why should the nations ask, “Where is their God?” Before our eyes, make known among the nations Your vengeance for the bloodshed of Your servants.

units.leftText: Let the sighing of the prisoner come before you. According to the greatness of your power, preserve those who are sentenced to death.
units.rightText: May the groans of the captives reach You; by the strength of Your arm preserve those condemned to death.

units.leftText: Pay back to our neighbors seven times into their bosom their reproach with which they have reproached you, Lord.
units.rightText: Pay back into the laps of our neighbors sevenfold the reproach they hurled at You, O Lord.

units.leftText: So we, your people and sheep of your pasture, will give you thanks forever. We will praise you forever, to all generations.
units.rightText: Then we Your people, the sheep of Your pasture, will thank You forever; from generation to generation we will declare Your praise.

units.leftText: Hear us, Shepherd of Israel, you who lead Joseph like a flock, you who sit above the cherubim, shine out.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Lilies of the Covenant.” A Psalm of Asaph. Hear us, O Shepherd of Israel, who leads Joseph like a flock; You who sit enthroned between the cherubim,

units.leftText: Before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, stir up your might! Come to save us!
units.rightText: before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. Rally Your mighty power and come to save us.

units.leftText: Turn us again, God. Cause your face to shine, and we will be saved.
units.rightText: Restore us, O God, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.

units.leftText: LORD God of Armies, how long will you be angry against the prayer of your people?
units.rightText: O LORD God of Hosts, how long will Your anger smolder against the prayers of Your people?

units.leftText: You have fed them with the bread of tears, and given them tears to drink in large measure.
units.rightText: You fed them with the bread of tears and made them drink the full measure of their tears.

units.leftText: You make us a source of contention to our neighbors. Our enemies laugh among themselves.
units.rightText: You make us contend with our neighbors; our enemies mock us.

units.leftText: Turn us again, God of Armies. Cause your face to shine, and we will be saved.
units.rightText: Restore us, O God of Hosts, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.

units.leftText: You brought a vine out of Egypt. You drove out the nations, and planted it.
units.rightText: You uprooted a vine from Egypt; You drove out the nations and transplanted it.

units.leftText: You cleared the ground for it. It took deep root, and filled the land.
units.rightText: You cleared the ground for it, and it took root and filled the land.

units.leftText: The mountains were covered with its shadow. Its boughs were like God’s cedars.
units.rightText: The mountains were covered by its shade, and the mighty cedars with its branches.

units.leftText: It sent out its branches to the sea, its shoots to the River.
units.rightText: It sent out its branches to the Sea, and its shoots toward the River.
rightNotes: 80:11 That is, the Mediterranean Sea, also called the Great Sea
80:11 That is, the Euphrates

units.leftText: Why have you broken down its walls, so that all those who pass by the way pluck it?
units.rightText: Why have You broken down its walls, so that all who pass by pick its fruit?

units.leftText: The boar out of the wood ravages it. The wild animals of the field feed on it.
units.rightText: The boar from the forest ravages it, and the creatures of the field feed upon it.

units.leftText: Turn again, we beg you, God of Armies. Look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vine,
units.rightText: Return, O God of Hosts, we pray! Look down from heaven and see! Attend to this vine—

units.leftText: the stock which your right hand planted, the branch that you made strong for yourself.
units.rightText: the root Your right hand has planted, the son You have raised up for Yourself.

units.leftText: It’s burned with fire. It’s cut down. They perish at your rebuke.
units.rightText: Your vine has been cut down and burned; they perish at the rebuke of Your countenance.

units.leftText: Let your hand be on the man of your right hand, on the son of man whom you made strong for yourself.
units.rightText: Let Your hand be upon the man at Your right hand, on the son of man You have raised up for Yourself.

units.leftText: So we will not turn away from you. Revive us, and we will call on your name.
units.rightText: Then we will not turn away from You; revive us, and we will call on Your name.

units.leftText: Turn us again, LORD God of Armies. Cause your face to shine, and we will be saved.
units.rightText: Restore us, O LORD God of Hosts; cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.

units.leftText: Sing aloud to God, our strength! Make a joyful shout to the God of Jacob!
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. Of Asaph. Sing for joy to God our strength; make a joyful noise to the God of Jacob.
rightNotes: 81:1 Gittith is probably a musical or liturgical term; here and in Psalms 8 and 84.

units.leftText: Raise a song, and bring here the tambourine, the pleasant lyre with the harp.
units.rightText: Lift up a song, strike the tambourine, play the sweet-sounding harp and lyre.

units.leftText: Blow the trumpet at the New Moon, at the full moon, on our feast day.
units.rightText: Sound the ram’s horn at the New Moon, and at the full moon on the day of our Feast.

units.leftText: For it is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob.
units.rightText: For this is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob.

units.leftText: He appointed it in Joseph for a covenant, when he went out over the land of Egypt, I heard a language that I didn’t know.
units.rightText: He ordained it as a testimony for Joseph when he went out over the land of Egypt, where I heard an unfamiliar language:
rightNotes: 81:5 Or in Joseph

units.leftText: “I removed his shoulder from the burden. His hands were freed from the basket.
units.rightText: “I relieved his shoulder of the burden; his hands were freed from the basket.

units.leftText: You called in trouble, and I delivered you. I answered you in the secret place of thunder. I tested you at the waters of Meribah.” Selah.*
units.rightText: You called out in distress, and I rescued you; I answered you from the cloud of thunder; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah
rightNotes: 81:7 Meribah means quarreling; see Exodus 17:7|EXO 17:7*.

units.leftText: “Hear, my people, and I will testify to you, Israel, if you would listen to me!
units.rightText: Hear, O My people, and I will warn you: O Israel, if only you would listen to Me!

units.leftText: There shall be no strange god in you, neither shall you worship any foreign god.
units.rightText: There must be no strange god among you, nor shall you bow to a foreign god.

units.leftText: I am the LORD, your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
units.rightText: I am the LORD your God, who brought you up out of Egypt. Open wide your mouth, and I will fill it.

units.leftText: But my people didn’t listen to my voice. Israel desired none of me.
units.rightText: But My people would not listen to Me, and Israel would not obey Me.

units.leftText: So I let them go after the stubbornness of their hearts, that they might walk in their own counsels.
units.rightText: So I gave them up to their stubborn hearts to follow their own devices.

units.leftText: Oh that my people would listen to me, that Israel would walk in my ways!
units.rightText: If only My people would listen to Me, if Israel would follow My ways,

units.leftText: I would soon subdue their enemies, and turn my hand against their adversaries.
units.rightText: how soon I would subdue their enemies and turn My hand against their foes!

units.leftText: The haters of the LORD would cringe before him, and their punishment would last forever.
units.rightText: Those who hate the LORD would feign obedience, and their doom would last forever.

units.leftText: But he would have also fed them with the finest of the wheat. I will satisfy you with honey out of the rock.”
units.rightText: But I would feed you the finest wheat; with honey from the rock I would satisfy you.”

units.leftText: God presides in the great assembly. He judges among the gods.
units.rightText: A Psalm of Asaph. God presides in the divine assembly; He renders judgment among the gods:

units.leftText: “How long will you judge unjustly, and show partiality to the wicked?” Selah.*
units.rightText: “How long will you judge unjustly and show partiality to the wicked? Selah
rightNotes: 82:2 Or How long will you defend the unjust

units.leftText: “Defend the weak, the poor, and the fatherless. Maintain the rights of the poor and oppressed.
units.rightText: Defend the cause of the weak and fatherless; uphold the rights of the afflicted and oppressed.

units.leftText: Rescue the weak and needy. Deliver them out of the hand of the wicked.”
units.rightText: Rescue the weak and needy; save them from the hand of the wicked.

units.leftText: They don’t know, neither do they understand. They walk back and forth in darkness. All the foundations of the earth are shaken.
units.rightText: They do not know or understand; they wander in the darkness; all the foundations of the earth are shaken.

units.leftText: I said, “You are gods, all of you are sons of the Most High.
units.rightText: I have said, ‘You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High.’
rightNotes: 82:6 Cited in John 10:34|JHN 10:34*

units.leftText: Nevertheless you shall die like men, and fall like one of the rulers.”
units.rightText: But like mortals you will die, and like rulers you will fall.”

units.leftText: Arise, God, judge the earth, for you inherit all of the nations.
units.rightText: Arise, O God, judge the earth, for all the nations are Your inheritance.

units.leftText: God, don’t keep silent. Don’t keep silent, and don’t be still, God.
units.rightText: A song. A Psalm of Asaph. O God, be not silent; be not speechless; be not still, O God.
rightNotes: 83:1 Or deaf

units.leftText: For, behold, your enemies are stirred up. Those who hate you have lifted up their heads.
units.rightText: See how Your enemies rage, how Your foes have reared their heads.

units.leftText: They conspire with cunning against your people. They plot against your cherished ones.
units.rightText: With cunning they scheme against Your people and conspire against those You cherish,

units.leftText: “Come,” they say, “let’s destroy them as a nation, that the name of Israel may be remembered no more.”
units.rightText: saying, “Come, let us erase them as a nation; may the name of Israel be remembered no more.”

units.leftText: For they have conspired together with one mind. They form an alliance against you.
units.rightText: For with one mind they plot together; they form an alliance against You—

units.leftText: The tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites; Moab, and the Hagrites;
units.rightText: the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, of Moab and the Hagrites,

units.leftText: Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek; Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre;
units.rightText: of Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, of Philistia with the people of Tyre.

units.leftText: Assyria also is joined with them. They have helped the children of Lot. Selah.*
units.rightText: Even Assyria has joined them, lending strength to the sons of Lot. Selah

units.leftText: Do to them as you did to Midian, as to Sisera, as to Jabin, at the river Kishon;
units.rightText: Do to them as You did to Midian, as to Sisera and Jabin at the River Kishon,

units.leftText: who perished at Endor, who became as dung for the earth.
units.rightText: who perished at Endor and became like dung on the ground.

units.leftText: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, yes, all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
units.rightText: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,

units.leftText: who said, “Let’s take possession of God’s pasture lands.”
units.rightText: who said, “Let us possess for ourselves the pastures of God.”

units.leftText: My God, make them like tumbleweed, like chaff before the wind.
units.rightText: Make them like tumbleweed, O my God, like chaff before the wind.

units.leftText: As the fire that burns the forest, as the flame that sets the mountains on fire,
units.rightText: As fire consumes a forest, as a flame sets the mountains ablaze,

units.leftText: so pursue them with your tempest, and terrify them with your storm.
units.rightText: so pursue them with Your tempest, and terrify them with Your storm.

units.leftText: Fill their faces with confusion, that they may seek your name, LORD.
units.rightText: Cover their faces with shame, that they may seek Your name, O LORD.

units.leftText: Let them be disappointed and dismayed forever. Yes, let them be confounded and perish;
units.rightText: May they be ever ashamed and terrified; may they perish in disgrace.

units.leftText: that they may know that you alone, whose name is the LORD, are the Most High over all the earth.
units.rightText: May they know that You alone, whose name is the LORD, are Most High over all the earth.
leftNotes: 83:18 LORD or GOD in all caps is from the Hebrew יהוה Yahweh except when otherwise noted as being from the short form יה Yah.

units.leftText: How lovely are your dwellings, LORD of Armies!
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. How lovely is Your dwelling place, O LORD of Hosts!
rightNotes: 84:1 Gittith is probably a musical or liturgical term; here and in Psalms 8 and 81.

units.leftText: My soul longs, and even faints for the courts of the LORD. My heart and my flesh cry out for the living God.
units.rightText: My soul longs, even faints, for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh cry out for the living God.

units.leftText: Yes, the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may have her young, near your altars, LORD of Armies, my King, and my God.
units.rightText: Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she places her young near Your altars, O LORD of Hosts, my King and my God.

units.leftText: Blessed are those who dwell in your house. They are always praising you. Selah.*
units.rightText: How blessed are those who dwell in Your house! They are ever praising You. Selah

units.leftText: Blessed are those whose strength is in you, who have set their hearts on a pilgrimage.
units.rightText: Blessed are those whose strength is in You, whose hearts are set on pilgrimage.

units.leftText: Passing through the valley of Weeping, they make it a place of springs. Yes, the autumn rain covers it with blessings.
units.rightText: As they pass through the Valley of Baca, they make it a place of springs; even the autumn rain covers it with pools.
rightNotes: 84:6 Or Valley of Poplars
84:6 Or with blessings

units.leftText: They go from strength to strength. Every one of them appears before God in Zion.
units.rightText: They go from strength to strength, until each appears before God in Zion.

units.leftText: LORD, God of Armies, hear my prayer. Listen, God of Jacob. Selah.*
units.rightText: O LORD God of Hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, O God of Jacob. Selah

units.leftText: Behold, God our shield, look at the face of your anointed.
units.rightText: Take notice of our shield, O God, and look with favor on the face of Your anointed.

units.leftText: For a day in your courts is better than a thousand. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
units.rightText: For better is one day in Your courts than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked.

units.leftText: For the LORD God is a sun and a shield. The LORD will give grace and glory. He withholds no good thing from those who walk blamelessly.
units.rightText: For the LORD God is a sun and a shield; the LORD gives grace and glory; He withholds no good thing from those who walk with integrity.

units.leftText: LORD of Armies, blessed is the man who trusts in you.
units.rightText: O LORD of Hosts, how blessed is the man who trusts in You!

units.leftText: LORD, you have been favorable to your land. You have restored the fortunes of Jacob.
units.rightText: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. You showed favor to Your land, O LORD; You restored Jacob from captivity.
rightNotes: 85:1 Or restored the fortunes of Jacob

units.leftText: You have forgiven the iniquity of your people. You have covered all their sin. Selah.*
units.rightText: You forgave the iniquity of Your people; You covered all their sin. Selah

units.leftText: You have taken away all your wrath. You have turned from the fierceness of your anger.
units.rightText: You withheld all Your fury; You turned from Your burning anger.

units.leftText: Turn us, God of our salvation, and cause your indignation toward us to cease.
units.rightText: Restore us, O God of our salvation, and put away Your displeasure toward us.

units.leftText: Will you be angry with us forever? Will you draw out your anger to all generations?
units.rightText: Will You be angry with us forever? Will You draw out Your anger to all generations?

units.leftText: Won’t you revive us again, that your people may rejoice in you?
units.rightText: Will You not revive us again, that Your people may rejoice in You?

units.leftText: Show us your loving kindness, LORD. Grant us your salvation.
units.rightText: Show us Your loving devotion, O LORD, and grant us Your salvation.

units.leftText: I will hear what God, the LORD, will speak, for he will speak peace to his people, his saints; but let them not turn again to folly.
units.rightText: I will listen to what God the LORD will say; for He will surely speak peace to His people and His saints; He will not let them return to folly.

units.leftText: Surely his salvation is near those who fear him, that glory may dwell in our land.
units.rightText: Surely His salvation is near to those who fear Him, that His glory may dwell in our land.

units.leftText: Mercy and truth meet together. Righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
units.rightText: Loving devotion and faithfulness have joined together; righteousness and peace have kissed.

units.leftText: Truth springs out of the earth. Righteousness has looked down from heaven.
units.rightText: Faithfulness sprouts from the earth, and righteousness looks down from heaven.

units.leftText: Yes, the LORD will give that which is good. Our land will yield its increase.
units.rightText: The LORD will indeed provide what is good, and our land will yield its increase.

units.leftText: Righteousness goes before him, and prepares the way for his steps.
units.rightText: Righteousness will go before Him to prepare the way for His steps.

units.leftText: Hear, LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.
units.rightText: A prayer of David. Incline Your ear, O LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.

units.leftText: Preserve my soul, for I am godly. You, my God, save your servant who trusts in you.
units.rightText: Preserve my soul, for I am godly. You are my God; save Your servant who trusts in You.

units.leftText: Be merciful to me, Lord, for I call to you all day long.
units.rightText: Be merciful to me, O Lord, for I call to You all day long.

units.leftText: Bring joy to the soul of your servant, for to you, Lord, do I lift up my soul.
units.rightText: Bring joy to Your servant, for to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul.

units.leftText: For you, Lord, are good, and ready to forgive, abundant in loving kindness to all those who call on you.
units.rightText: For You, O Lord, are kind and forgiving, rich in loving devotion to all who call on You.

units.leftText: Hear, LORD, my prayer. Listen to the voice of my petitions.
units.rightText: Hear my prayer, O LORD, and attend to my plea for mercy.

units.leftText: In the day of my trouble I will call on you, for you will answer me.
units.rightText: In the day of my distress I call on You, because You answer me.

units.leftText: There is no one like you among the gods, Lord, nor any deeds like your deeds.
units.rightText: O Lord, there is none like You among the gods, nor any works like Yours.

units.leftText: All nations you have made will come and worship before you, Lord. They shall glorify your name.
units.rightText: All the nations You have made will come and bow before You, O Lord, and they will glorify Your name.

units.leftText: For you are great, and do wondrous things. You are God alone.
units.rightText: For You are great and perform wonders; You alone are God.

units.leftText: Teach me your way, LORD. I will walk in your truth. Make my heart undivided to fear your name.
units.rightText: Teach me Your way, O LORD, that I may walk in Your truth. Give me an undivided heart, that I may fear Your name.

units.leftText: I will praise you, Lord my God, with my whole heart. I will glorify your name forever more.
units.rightText: I will praise You, O Lord my God, with all my heart; I will glorify Your name forever.

units.leftText: For your loving kindness is great toward me. You have delivered my soul from the lowest Sheol.
units.rightText: For great is Your loving devotion to me; You have delivered me from the depths of Sheol.
leftNotes: 86:13 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: God, the proud have risen up against me. A company of violent men have sought after my soul, and they don’t hold regard for you before them.
units.rightText: The arrogant rise against me, O God; a band of ruthless men seeks my life; they have no regard for You.

units.leftText: But you, Lord, are a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth.
units.rightText: But You, O Lord, are a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion and faithfulness.

units.leftText: Turn to me, and have mercy on me! Give your strength to your servant. Save the son of your servant.
units.rightText: Turn to me and have mercy; grant Your strength to Your servant; save the son of Your maidservant.

units.leftText: Show me a sign of your goodness, that those who hate me may see it, and be shamed, because you, LORD, have helped me, and comforted me.
units.rightText: Show me a sign of Your goodness, that my enemies may see and be ashamed; for You, O LORD, have helped me and comforted me.

units.leftText: His foundation is in the holy mountains.
units.rightText: A Psalm of the sons of Korah. A song. He has founded His city on the holy mountains.
rightNotes: 87:1 Literally His foundation is on the holy mountains

units.leftText: The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
units.rightText: The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.

units.leftText: Glorious things are spoken about you, city of God. Selah.*
units.rightText: Glorious things are ascribed to you, O city of God. Selah

units.leftText: I will record Rahab and Babylon among those who acknowledge me. Behold, Philistia, Tyre, and also Ethiopia: “This one was born there.”
units.rightText: “I will mention Rahab and Babylon among those who know Me — along with Philistia, Tyre, and Cush — when I say, ‘This one was born in Zion.’”
leftNotes: 87:4 Rahab is a reference to Egypt.
rightNotes: 87:4 Rahab is a poetic name for Egypt.
87:4 That is, the upper Nile region

units.leftText: Yes, of Zion it will be said, “This one and that one was born in her;” the Most High himself will establish her.
units.rightText: And it will be said of Zion: “This one and that one were born in her, and the Most High Himself will establish her.”

units.leftText: The LORD will count, when he writes up the peoples, “This one was born there.” Selah.*
units.rightText: The LORD will record in the register of the peoples: “This one was born in Zion.” Selah

units.leftText: Those who sing as well as those who dance say, “All my springs are in you.”
units.rightText: Singers and pipers will proclaim, “All my springs of joy are in You.”

units.leftText: LORD, the God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before you.
units.rightText: A song. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. For the choirmaster. According to Mahalath Leannoth. A Maskil of Heman the Ezrahite. O LORD, the God of my salvation, day and night I cry out before You.
rightNotes: 88:1 Mahalath Leannothis probably a musical or liturgical term; see also Psalm 53:1|PSA 53:1*.
88:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142.

units.leftText: Let my prayer enter into your presence. Turn your ear to my cry.
units.rightText: May my prayer come before You; incline Your ear to my cry.

units.leftText: For my soul is full of troubles. My life draws near to Sheol.
units.rightText: For my soul is full of troubles, and my life draws near to Sheol.
leftNotes: 88:3 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: I am counted among those who go down into the pit. I am like a man who has no help,
units.rightText: I am counted among those descending to the Pit. I am like a man without strength.

units.leftText: set apart among the dead, like the slain who lie in the grave, whom you remember no more. They are cut off from your hand.
units.rightText: I am forsaken among the dead, like the slain who lie in the grave, whom You remember no more, who are cut off from Your care.

units.leftText: You have laid me in the lowest pit, in the darkest depths.
units.rightText: You have laid me in the lowest Pit, in the darkest of the depths.

units.leftText: Your wrath lies heavily on me. You have afflicted me with all your waves. Selah.*
units.rightText: Your wrath weighs heavily upon me; all Your waves have submerged me. Selah

units.leftText: You have taken my friends from me. You have made me an abomination to them. I am confined, and I can’t escape.
units.rightText: You have removed my friends from me; You have made me repulsive to them; I am confined and cannot escape.

units.leftText: My eyes are dim from grief. I have called on you daily, LORD. I have spread out my hands to you.
units.rightText: My eyes grow dim with grief. I call to You daily, O LORD; I spread out my hands to You.

units.leftText: Do you show wonders to the dead? Do the departed spirits rise up and praise you? Selah.*
units.rightText: Do You work wonders for the dead? Do departed spirits rise up to praise You? Selah

units.leftText: Is your loving kindness declared in the grave? Or your faithfulness in Destruction?
units.rightText: Can Your loving devotion be proclaimed in the grave, Your faithfulness in Abaddon ?
rightNotes: 88:11 Abaddon means Destruction.

units.leftText: Are your wonders made known in the dark? Or your righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?
units.rightText: Will Your wonders be known in the darkness, or Your righteousness in the land of oblivion?

units.leftText: But to you, LORD, I have cried. In the morning, my prayer comes before you.
units.rightText: But to You, O LORD, I cry for help; in the morning my prayer comes before You.

units.leftText: LORD, why do you reject my soul? Why do you hide your face from me?
units.rightText: Why, O LORD, do You reject me? Why do You hide Your face from me?

units.leftText: I am afflicted and ready to die from my youth up. While I suffer your terrors, I am distracted.
units.rightText: From my youth I was afflicted and near death. I have borne Your terrors; I am in despair.

units.leftText: Your fierce wrath has gone over me. Your terrors have cut me off.
units.rightText: Your wrath has swept over me; Your terrors have destroyed me.

units.leftText: They came around me like water all day long. They completely engulfed me.
units.rightText: All day long they engulf me like water; they enclose me on every side.

units.leftText: You have put lover and friend far from me, and my friends into darkness.
units.rightText: You have removed my beloved and my friend; darkness is my closest companion.

units.leftText: I will sing of the loving kindness of the LORD forever. With my mouth, I will make known your faithfulness to all generations.
units.rightText: A Maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite. I will sing of the loving devotion of the LORD forever; with my mouth I will proclaim Your faithfulness to all generations.
rightNotes: 89:1 Maskil is probably a musical or liturgical term; used for Psalms 32, 42, 44–45, 52–55, 74, 78, 88–89, and 142.

units.leftText: I indeed declare, “Love stands firm forever. You established the heavens. Your faithfulness is in them.”
units.rightText: For I have said, “Loving devotion is built up forever; in the heavens You establish Your faithfulness.”

units.leftText: “I have made a covenant with my chosen one, I have sworn to David, my servant,
units.rightText: You said, “I have made a covenant with My chosen one, I have sworn to David My servant:

units.leftText: ‘I will establish your offspring forever, and build up your throne to all generations.’” Selah.*
units.rightText: ‘I will establish your offspring forever and build up your throne for all generations.’” Selah

units.leftText: The heavens will praise your wonders, LORD, your faithfulness also in the assembly of the holy ones.
units.rightText: The heavens praise Your wonders, O LORD — Your faithfulness as well — in the assembly of the holy ones.

units.leftText: For who in the skies can be compared to the LORD? Who among the sons of the heavenly beings is like the LORD,
units.rightText: For who in the skies can compare with the LORD? Who among the heavenly beings is like the LORD?
rightNotes: 89:6 Or the sons of God or the sons of might

units.leftText: a very awesome God in the council of the holy ones, to be feared above all those who are around him?
units.rightText: In the council of the holy ones, God is greatly feared, and awesome above all who surround Him.

units.leftText: LORD, God of Armies, who is a mighty one, like you? LORD, your faithfulness is around you.
units.rightText: O LORD God of Hosts, who is like You? O mighty LORD, Your faithfulness surrounds You.
leftNotes: 89:8 LORD or GOD in all caps is from the Hebrew יהוה Yahweh except when otherwise noted as being from the short form יה Yah.
89:8 Hebrew: יה Yah

units.leftText: You rule the pride of the sea. When its waves rise up, you calm them.
units.rightText: You rule the raging sea; when its waves mount up, You still them.

units.leftText: You have broken Rahab in pieces, like one of the slain. You have scattered your enemies with your mighty arm.
units.rightText: You crushed Rahab like a carcass; You scattered Your enemies with Your mighty arm.

units.leftText: The heavens are yours. The earth also is yours, the world and its fullness. You have founded them.
units.rightText: The heavens are Yours, and also the earth. The earth and its fullness You founded.

units.leftText: You have created the north and the south. Tabor and Hermon rejoice in your name.
units.rightText: North and south You created; Tabor and Hermon shout for joy at Your name.

units.leftText: You have a mighty arm. Your hand is strong, and your right hand is exalted.
units.rightText: Mighty is Your arm; strong is Your hand. Your right hand is exalted.

units.leftText: Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne. Loving kindness and truth go before your face.
units.rightText: Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne; loving devotion and faithfulness go before You.

units.leftText: Blessed are the people who learn to acclaim you. They walk in the light of your presence, LORD.
